1:1.t: If in the explanations of all the prophets we need the coming of the Holy Spirit, so that they may be opened by the revelation of him by whose prompting they were written; and if in Isaiah and in the Apocalypse we read of a sealed book, which the scribes and Pharisees, who boast that they know the letters of the law, cannot read, because it is sealed, and no one could be found who could unlock its mysteries except the lion of the tribe of Judah, whom God the Father has sealed: how much more, in the explanation of the prophet Hosea, must the Lord be prayed to, and must we say with Peter: Explain this parable to us. Especially since he who wrote it himself testifies at the end to the obscurity of the volume: Who is wise, and he will understand these things, understanding, and he will know them? This we ought to take not as something impossible but as something difficult, according to that saying of the Gospel: Who, do you think, is the faithful and prudent servant whom the Lord has set over his household? […]

The word of the Lord which came to Hosea son of Beeri. LXX: likewise. The Word of the Lord (which in the beginning was with God the Father, and the Word was God) came to Hosea son of Beeri, so as to make the prophet too a god, as the Savior says: If he called them gods to whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken, him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world you tell: You blaspheme; because I said, I am the Son of God. So that, just as God makes gods, and stands in the synagogue of gods, and in the midst he judges between gods; and, though he himself is the true light, which enlightens every man coming into this world, says to the apostles: You are the light of the world, so too the Savior himself may make his prophet a savior. For Hosea, in our language, means savior, a name which Joshua son of Nun also had before his name was changed by God. For he was not called — as is wrongly read in the Greek and Latin manuscripts — Ause, which means nothing at all; but Hoshea, that is, savior; […]

1:2.t: It is asked why Ezekiel refused easier things, while Hosea was at once joined to a harlot and did not object, or rather reply, that he had a chaste body and ought not to be stained by union with a prostitute, as the Apostle says: He who cleaves to a prostitute becomes one body with her; from this it is shown that it was a figure of the Synagogue or of the Church, not truly carried out according to the letter, as we discussed more fully when expounding that prophet himself.

The beginning of the Lord's speaking in Hosea. LXX: The beginning of the word of the Lord to Hosea. Because, as we said above, Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, in whose reigns they prophesied, are set at the head of the title of other prophets too, he therefore now says that among all these the Lord spoke first in Hosea, and afterwards to the rest. But it is one thing for the Lord to speak in Hosea, another to speak to Hosea. In Hosea, he does not speak to Hosea himself, but through Hosea to others; but when he speaks to Hosea, he is signified to address his discourse to Hosea himself. Others, however, do not want Hosea to have been the first of all the prophets on the ground of what is said: The beginning of the Lord's speaking in Hosea; but hold that it shows that the Lord spoke these things which follow first to Hosea.

And the Lord said to Hosea: Go, take for yourself a wife of fornications and children of fornications, for the land, fornicating, will commit fornication away from the Lord. […]

Against conjugal chastity it is objected: every act and movement that alienates from God is foreign to virtue: but the act of conjugal continence is such: therefore it is foreign to virtue. Proof of the middle term: Hosea 1; the Gloss: "Just as wine intoxicates a man and alienates him from the state of his mind, so the law of marriage alienates a man from the things that are of God."

To this it must be said that something is said to alienate from God in two ways: either simply, or with respect to some act or state. In the first way it cannot be without sin: in the second way it can be through the punishment of sin and also through an act of virtue: just as the exercise of action retards and for a time impedes the act of contemplation, just as also sleep impedes the exercise in virtue.
1:2.s: Disputed Questions on Evangelical Perfection, Question 3

1:3.t: Gomer is interpreted τετελεσμένην, that is, consummated and perfected; others think that θώρακας, that is, breastplates, is signified. There are some who suppose it means measure, or bitterness, which they would say rightly if it did not have the letter gimel. Diblaim means παλάτας (cakes of pressed figs), of which there is a very great abundance in Palestine, and which the prophet Isaiah is commanded to apply to the ulcer of king Hezekiah. It is a mass of rich dried figs, which they shape after the manner of bricks, tread and press together, so that they may remain long unspoiled.

And he went and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim; and she conceived and bore him a son. And the Lord said to him: Call his name Jezreel, for yet a little while and I will visit the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu; and I will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease. LXX: And he went, and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim; and she conceived and bore a son. And the Lord said to him: Call his name Jezreel, because yet a little while and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Judah; and I will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease. The prophets make their promises about the coming of Christ and the calling of the Gentiles many ages later in such a way as not to neglect the present time, lest they seem not to teach an assembly called together for another purpose about the things that are at hand, but to trifle about things uncertain and future. […]

1:4.t: Therefore Israel too, consummated and perfected in fornication, a daughter of pleasure, which seems sweet and pleasant to those who enjoy it, is taken as wife by Hosea as a type of the Lord Savior; and from her a son of God is first begotten, that is, Jezreel; and this is the metropolis of the ten tribes, in which Naboth was killed, on account of whose blood Jehu is raised up, who destroyed the house of Ahab and Jezebel. But because Jehu himself too, the avenger of just blood, walked in the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel commit fornication and set up golden calves in Dan and Bethel, his kingdom too is said to be overturned; under his great-grandson Jeroboam Hosea began to prophesy; when he died, his son Zechariah succeeded to the kingdom; and in the sixth month of his rule Shallum, born of another stock, killed him. […]

1:4.s: On Hebrew Names, On Hosea the Prophet

1:5.t: And on that day I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel. LXX: likewise. When I have avenged the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and have destroyed the kingdom of Israel through the victory of the Assyrian, then on that day and at that time I will break all the strength of the army of Israel in the valley of Jezreel. We said above that Jezreel, which is now near Maximianopolis, was the metropolis of the kingdom of Samaria; near it are very broad plains, and a valley of exceeding vastness, which stretches for more than ten thousand paces. In this valley, when battle was joined, Israel was cut down by the Assyrians, that is, the ten tribes, which, on account of Jeroboam of the tribe of Ephraim, who first made a schism among the people, were called Ephraim. Sometimes, on account of Joseph, who was the father of Ephraim, it is called Joseph; […]

1:6.t: And she conceived again and bore a daughter; and he said to him: Call her name: Without Mercy; for I will no more have mercy on the house of Israel, but with forgetting I will forget them. And on the house of Judah I will have mercy; and I will save them in the Lord their God; and I will not save them by bow and sword, and by war, and by horses, and by horsemen. LXX: And she conceived again and bore a daughter, and he said to him: Call her name: Without Mercy; for by no means will I any more have mercy on the house of Israel, but opposing I will oppose them; but on the sons of Judah I will have mercy, and I will save them in the Lord their God; and I will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by war, nor by horses, nor by horsemen. After the bow of Israel was crushed and broken in the valley of Jezreel, and the kingdom of the ten tribes was forsaken, so that they were led into captivity, there is no longer born a Jezreel, that is, the seed of God, nor a son of the male sex; […]

According to the type, we say that those who, on account of the blood of the seed of God, are called: Without Mercy, and dared to say: His blood be upon us, and upon our children, serve the Romans to this day; but that the house of Judah, namely those of the Jews who confessed the Lord, were saved not by the strength of an army but by the preaching of the Gospel. What we have interpreted of Israel and Judah, both according to the history and according to the type, let us refer to the conventicles of the heretics and to the Church of the Lord Savior: that, while they are left without mercy and lose their kingdom, the Church has prevailed by the power of her God.

For οὐκ ἠλεημένη, that is, without mercy, in some copies is found οὐκ ἠγαπημένη, that is, not beloved. But the truer copies are those which have without mercy; especially since, to distinguish it from Israel, on whom he has no mercy, God adds: But on the house of Judah I will have mercy.

1:7.t: Why, then, should we hesitate to say what Scripture does not shrink from declaring? Why shall the truth of faith hesitate in that wherein the authority of Scripture has never hesitated? For, behold, Hosea the prophet says in the person of the Father: "I will not now save them by bow, nor by horses, nor by horsemen; but I will save them by the Lord their God." If God says that He saves by God, still God does not save except by Christ. Why, then, should man hesitate to call Christ God, when he observes that He is declared to be God by the Father according to the Scriptures? Yea, if God the Father does not save except by God, no one can be saved by God the Father unless he shall have confessed Christ to be God, in whom and by whom the Father promises that He will give him salvation: so that, reasonably, whoever acknowledges Him to be God, may find salvation in Christ God; whoever does not acknowledge Him to be God, would lose salvation which he could not find elsewhere than in Christ God.

For He says to Hosea the prophet, "I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel, but will altogether be their enemy. But I will have mercy upon the children of Judah, and will save them in the Lord their God." Here God the Father gives the name of God, without any ambiguity, to the Son, in Whom also He chose us before countless ages. "Their God," He says, for while the Father, being Unoriginate, is independent of all, He has given us for an inheritance to His Son. In like manner we read, "Ask of Me, and I will give Thee the Gentiles for Thine inheritance." None can be God to Him from Whom are all things, for He is eternal and has no beginning; but the Son has God, from Whom He was born, for His Father. Yet to us the Father is God and the Son is God; the Father reveals to us that the Son is our God, and the Son teaches that the Father is God over us. The point for us to remember is that in this passage the Father gives to the Son the name of God, the title of His own unoriginate majesty.

But to the house of Judah he promises mercy, and says that he saves them in the Lord their God, either in himself who speaks; or the Father saves in the Son, according to what is written: The Lord rained from the Lord. For when Israel was handed over to the Assyrians, he saved them from the hand of Sennacherib, not by bow and sword and war and by a multitude of horsemen, but by his own strength, when he sent an angel and struck down from the army of Sennacherib king of the Assyrians in one night one hundred and eighty-five thousand.

1:8.t: And she weaned her who was Without Mercy; and she conceived and bore a son; and he said: Call his name Not My People, for you are not my people and I will not be yours. LXX: likewise. He who was called the seed of God, turned into a female and, because of the weakness of his strength and the offense of God, led into captivity, since he did not have the mercy of the Lord, is said to have been weaned not as a son but as a daughter; for the man had already lost his vigor. Whoever is weaned withdraws from the mother, no longer feeds on the parent's milk, and is sustained by food from outside. So also Israel, cast off by the Lord, hemmed in by the straits of captivity, and in Babylon sustained by unclean foods, is called not the people of God, and is struck with the eternal sentence of a foreign nation, so that he is called Not My People and is disowned forever. […]

1:9.t:
Finally, whoever wishes fuller proof that mere words are nothing without actions should consider how countless peoples, by failing in good works, have lost the names given them. The twelve tribes of the Hebrews, when they were of old chosen by God, received two holy names, for they were called the people of God, and Israel. We read: "Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against thee." Once the Jews bore both these titles, now they have neither. They who long since left off the worship of God cannot be called God's people, nor can they who denied his Son be given a name that means "Seeing God." So it is written: "But Israel does not know, my people doth not consider."

For this reason on another occasion our God spoke of the people of the Hebrews to the prophet, saying: "Call his name, Not Beloved." And speaking to the Jews themselves: "You are not my people and I am not your God." […]
1:9.s: On the Government of God, Book 4, Chapter 1

1:10.t: And the number of the sons of Israel will be like the sand of the sea, which is without measure and will not be numbered. And it will be in the place where it will be said to them: You are not my people, it will be said to them: Sons of the living God. And the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel will be gathered together; and they will set over themselves one head and will go up from the land, for great is the day of Jezreel. LXX: And the number of the sons of Israel will be as the sand of the sea, which will not be measured nor can be numbered. And it will be in the place where it was said to them: You are not my people, they will be called sons of the living God. And the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel will be gathered together; and they will set over themselves one rule, and will go up from the land, for great is the day of Jezreel. We have read of the casting off of the ten tribes, and of Israel, not to be measured and no longer the people of God, condemned by perpetual indignation. […]

2:1.t: Say to your brothers: My People, and to your sister: Obtained Mercy. LXX: Say to your brother: My People, and to your sister: Obtained Mercy. Since great is the day of Jezreel, in which Judah and Israel had one prince, and it will by no means be said to Israel: Not My People; but on the contrary they will be called sons of the living God. Therefore, O men of the tribe of Judah, do not despair of the salvation of the ten tribes, but daily, by word and by prayer and by letters, call them to repentance, because he is called your brother and your sister: brother from the fact that he is called My People; sister from the fact that he is named Obtained Mercy. Otherwise: you who believe in Christ, and are as much from the Jews as from the Gentiles, say to the broken branches, and to the former people which was cast off: My People, because he is your brother; and Obtained Mercy, because she is your sister. For when the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, then all Israel will be saved. […]

2:2.t: Judge your mother, judge, since she is not my wife and I am not her husband; let her put away her fornications from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts, lest perhaps I strip her naked and set her as on the day of her birth. LXX: Be judged with your mother, be judged, because she is not my wife and I am not her husband; and I will put away her fornication from my face, and her adulteries from between her breasts, so that I may strip her naked, and restore her as on the day of her birth. Up to this point the discourse has been directed to the people of Israel, that is, to the ten tribes. Now another section begins, and the sons, that is, the people, are commanded to enter into judgment against their mother, who bore them, who, made a wife from a harlot, did not abandon her former ways, and again played the harlot with her lovers. And see the clemency of the husband. She has already been repudiated, already cast off; he has already said to her: She is not my wife and I am not her husband; […]

The Synagogue is both of these, and if she persists in fornication and adultery, God will take away from her the garments and ornaments which he had given. Of these Ezekiel writes: On the day when you were born, they did not bind your breasts, and you were not salted with salt: and I passed by you, and found you naked, and disfigured, and spattered with blood. And a little after: I clothed you with fine linen and delicate stuffs, and placed ornaments about you, and gave bracelets about your hands, a necklace about your neck. These things her most generous husband gave her then, when he found her in Egypt, defiled by the lust of idolatry and spreading her feet for all. And now he threatens that, if she will not return to her husband, she will be without God and husband, just as she had been before in Egypt. […]

2:3.t: And I will make her like a wilderness, and set her like a pathless land, and kill her with thirst. LXX: And I will make her as a desert, and set her as a land without water, and slay her in thirst. If she will not be converted to better things, I will do to her what I did in the wilderness, so that, led into captivity, they may fall in a foreign land, suffering thirst for all good things, and be unable to return to their homeland. Or at least let them hear in the Gospel: Your house will be left to you desolate. And the Lord will send them not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water; but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord. Of which Isaiah also speaks: They will be like a garden that has no water. The heretics who have been cast off by the Lord, if they do not return to their former home, will suffer such want of all things that even what they seem to have, though false, will be reduced to nothing.

2:4.t: And on her children I will have no mercy, since they are children of fornications, for their mother has played the harlot. She who conceived them is confounded, for she said: I will go after my lovers, who give me bread and my waters, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink. LXX: And on her children I will have no mercy, since they are children of fornication, for their mother has played the harlot. She who bore them is confounded; for she said: I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, and my garments and my linens, and my oil and all things that are necessary to me. This I will do besides to her to whom I said: not my wife, and I am not your husband, and I will make her like a wilderness, and make her like a pathless land. For when I led her out of Egypt, the parents were slain and their sons entered the land of promise. But now the children of the fornicating mother will perish with their harlot mother, since they are children of fornication, and evil ones begotten of evil ones. […]

2:5.t: Is not this the mark of a hard brow and of a harlot's shamelessness, to glory in one's own crime and say: I will follow my lovers; I will go to the idols which have supplied me with what is necessary both for food and for clothing? All the things which the prophetic word describes the Jews received spiritually from the Lord. And because they denied the Son of God, choosing for themselves Barabbas, the author of robbery and sedition, and crucifying the Son of God, therefore to this day they follow demons, and ascribe the benefits of God to those who have destroyed the souls of their worshippers. The heretics have bread and waters: their bread is the bread of mourning, and their waters are muddy, waters which choke and kill the baptized. […]

Who is that adulterous woman whom the prophet Hosea points out, who said, "I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, and everything that befits me?" Let us grant that we may understand this also of the people of the Jews that went astray; yet whom else are the false Christians (such as are all heretics and schismatics) wont to imitate, except false Israelites?

They, therefore, who are wicked, evildoers, carnal, fleshly, devilish, think that they receive at the hands of their seducers what are the gifts of God alone, whether sacraments, or any spiritual workings about present salvation. But these men have not love towards God, but are busied about those by whose pride they are led astray, and are compared to the adulterous woman, whom the prophet introduces as saying, "I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, and my oil, and everything that befits me." For thus arise heresies and schisms, when the fleshly people which is not founded on the love of God says, "I will go after my lovers," with whom, either by corruption of her faith, or by the puffing up of her pride, she shamefully commits adultery. […]

And hence it comes that for the most part when instead of good things we ask for the opposite, our prayer is either heard but tardily or not at all; and again the Lord vouchsafes to bring upon us even against our will, like some most beneficent physician, for our good what we think is opposed to it, and sometimes He delays and hinders our injurious purposes and deadly attempts from having their horrible effects, and, while we are rushing headlong towards death, draws us back to salvation, and rescues us without our knowing it from the jaws of hell.

And this care of His and providence with regard to us the Divine word has finely described by the prophet Hosea under the figure of Jerusalem as an harlot, and inclining with disgraceful eagerness to the worship of idols, where when she says: "I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread, and my water, and my wool, and my flax, and my oil, and my drink;" […]
2:5.s: The Third Conference of Abbot Chaeremon, Chapters 7-8

2:6.t: And also in Hosea, where it is said of Jerusalem committing fornication: Behold, I will close her ways with thorns, and I will block up her paths, and she will not find her track, and she will pursue her lovers, and will not overtake them, and she will seek them, and will not find them; and she will say: I will go and return to my former husband, for it was better with me then than now. Notice that unless the ways had been closed and the paths fenced off, and unless the Lord had destroyed her ways, the fornicating soul could never have said: I will go and return to my former husband.

But if, following the sense above, we wish to take Now the daughter shall be blocked with a blockade as said of the Church, let us bring forward that example from Hosea, in which the adulteress speaks: I will go after my lovers, who gave me my bread, and my water, and my garments, and my linens, my oil, and all things that profit me. And afterwards God, wishing to hinder her most wicked thought, does not let her fulfill what she desires, but blocks her ways, so that she may not overtake her lovers and commit fornication further. For he says: Therefore, behold, I will block her ways with stakes, and I will hedge up her ways, and she will not find her path; and she will pursue her lovers, and will not lay hold of them, and she will seek them, and will not find them, and she will say: I will go and return to my former husband, because it was well with me. […]

Because of this, behold, I will hedge up your way with thorns, and I will hedge it with a wall, and she will not find her paths, and she will follow her lovers and will not overtake them, and she will seek them and will not find them, and she will say: I will go and return to my first husband, for it was well with me then, more than now. LXX: Therefore, behold, I will hedge up her way with stakes, and I will block her ways; and she will not find her path. And she will pursue her lovers, and will not overtake them; and she will seek them and will not find them; and she will say: I will go and return to my first husband, for it was better with me then than it is now. The harlot had said: I will go after my lovers, who have supplied me with abundance of all things. […]

For hence is that which the Lord says, under the character of every soul, to Judaea who is weak, and walking in evil ways; "Behold, I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and I will hedge it up with a wall, and she shall not find her paths, and she shall follow after her lovers, and she shall not overtake them, and she shall seek them, and not finding them shall say, I will go and return to my first husband, for then it was better with me than now." For the ways of the Elect are hedged up with thorns, when they find the pain of piercing in that which they desire in this world. He obstructs, as it were, by interposing a wall, the ways of those, whose desires the difficulty of attainment opposes. Their souls truly seek their lovers, and find them not, when by following malignant spirits, they do not gain hold of those pleasures of this world, which they desire. But it is well added that she says immediately in consequence of this very difficulty; […]
2:6.s: Morals on the Book of Job, Book 34:3

2:6.t: For there are some who understand the good things they ought to do, but cease from doing them; they see what they ought to do, but do not follow it out of desire. To these, as we said above, it often happens that the adversity of this world strikes them in their carnal desires; they try to grasp temporal glory and cannot; and while they propose to sail through the deep waters, as it were, toward the greater concerns of this age, they are always driven back by contrary winds to the shores of their own dejection. And when they see themselves broken in their desires, with the world opposing them, they are reminded what they owe to their Creator, so that they return to Him with shame, whom they had abandoned in their pride for love of the world. […]

Concerning such people the Lord speaks to the prophet under the figure of Jerusalem, saying: Behold, I will hedge your way with thorns, and I will fence it with a wall, and she will not find her paths. And she will follow her lovers and will not overtake them; she will seek them and will not find them (Hosea 2:6). Our lovers are carnal desires; we follow our lovers when we labor in this, that we may become possessors of riches, so that we may have the means to satisfy carnal desires. We follow our lovers and do not overtake them when, with the mercy of God preventing us, we are not able to reach that which we uselessly desire.

2:7.t: So, then, understand that your soul too has had many lovers, who delighted in her beauty, with whom she played the harlot. Concerning whom she also said: "I will go after my lovers, who give me my wine and my oil", and the rest. But now she has come to that time when she says: "I will return to my former husband, because it was better for me then than now". You have returned, then, to your former husband; without doubt you have given offense to your lovers, with whom you were committing adulteries. Unless, therefore, you now abide with your husband in whole faith, and are glued to him with your whole love, out of the many crimes which you have committed every movement of yours and glance of yours is suspect to him, and your very gait, if it be too careless. He can see nothing further in you that is wanton, nothing dissolute and prodigal. But when you turn your eyes even a little away from your husband, at once there must needs come a remembrance of former things. […]

2:8.t: And she did not know this, that I gave her grain and wine and oil, and multiplied silver for her, and gold, which they made into Baal. LXX: And she did not know that I gave her grain and wine and oil, and multiplied silver for her; but these she made into things of silver and gold for Baal. He is answering what came before, for she had said: I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, wool and flax, and my oil and my drink; all of which she had received so that she might turn them to the worship of God. But she, the bread that strengthens and the wine that gladdens the heart of man, and the oil that enlightens every man coming into this world, and the silver of which we have often said: The words of the Lord, chaste words, silver tested by fire, proved for the earth, purified sevenfold; […]

2:9.t: For an unclean spirit dwelt in us before we believed, before we came to Christ, when still, as I said above, our soul was fornicating away from God and was with its lovers, the demons. But after she said: "I will return to my former husband" and came to Christ, who from the beginning "created her according to his own image", the adulterous spirit necessarily gave place when it saw the lawful husband. We have been received, then, by Christ, and our house has been "cleansed" from former sins and "adorned" with the ornaments of the sacraments of the faithful, which those who have been initiated know. But this house does not at once merit to have Christ as its inhabitant, unless its life and conduct be so holy, so pure and undefiled, that it may merit to be a "temple of God". For it must be no longer a house, but a temple, in which God may dwell. If, then, it neglect the grace received and entangle itself in worldly affairs, straightway that unclean spirit returns and claims for itself the empty house.

Therefore I will return and take my grain in its time, and my wine in its time, and I will set free my wool and my flax, which covered her disgrace. LXX: Therefore I will return and take away my wheat in its time, and my wine in its time, and I will take away my garments and my linens, so that they may not cover her disgrace. The punishment is heavier when, at the time of harvest and vintage, the hoped-for crops and the wine are taken away, and are, as it were, snatched out of the hands that already held them. But if at the time of the threshing floor and the vat and the winepress, when the earth makes up for past barrenness with new crops, there is a want of all things, what must we reckon of the rest of the year, when the old stores too are being saved? Now the wool and the flax, or the garments and the linens, are set free, so that they may no longer cover the harlot's disgrace; that is to say, so that she may be stripped of God's help, and the protection of all the angels may depart from her. […]

2:10.t: So then, once the garment and the linen have been set free, so that they might no longer cover the disgrace of the fornicating woman, all the shame of Jerusalem, or the folly through which she worked shame, will be uncovered in the sight of her lovers, so that those who desired her veiled may despise her exposed. And when she has been handed over to her lovers the Assyrians, or to the demons whom both she herself and the Assyrians serve, no one, he says, will be able to snatch her from my hand; for the weakness of the demons is proved in this, that those whom they had received abounding in all things they cannot free when they are crushed by evils.

These things, both according to the history and according to tropology, unhappy Judea has suffered: all her shame has been uncovered in the eyes of the Gentiles, and no one could rescue her from the hands of God. All the ceremonies have ceased, the festivity has been turned into mourning; all that she thought was given her by the demons, she now knows has been taken away because she offended God. First the Assyrians and the Chaldeans devoured her, the Medes and the Persians and the Macedonians; at the last the most savage beast tore her apart, the empire of the Romans, whose name is passed over in silence in Daniel, so that the dread of those who are to be devoured may be made greater. What we have said of Judea, refer to the heretics, who, promising doctrine and knowledge at first sight, having gone out from the Church, are deserted by God; and all their disgrace is set in the sight of their lovers, whom they had deceived before; […]

2:11.t: And handed over to Babylonian slavery, she will by no means be able to celebrate the three solemnities of Passover and Pentecost and Tabernacles, nor to keep the joy of the new moon, that is, of the calends, nor of the sabbath, nor all the festivals, which he comprises under one name.

2:12.t: And now I will uncover her folly in the eyes of her lovers; and no one will rescue her from my hand and I will make all her joy cease, her solemnity, her new moon, her sabbath, and all her festal times; and I will spoil her vine and her fig tree, of which she said: These are my wages, which my lovers gave me; and I will make her into a forest, and the beast of the field will eat her. LXX: And now I will uncover her uncleanness in the sight of her lovers; and no one will rescue her from my hand; and I will turn away all her gladness, her solemnities and her new moons, and the sabbaths, and all her festivals; and I will destroy her vine, and her fig trees, of which she said: These are my wages which my lovers gave me; and I will make her a testimony, and the beasts of the field will eat her. What follows, The birds of the sky and the creeping things of the earth, must be marked beforehand with an obelus. […]

The vine too and the fig tree and the abundance of all things will be spoiled: in the vine understand gladness, in the fig sweetness and pleasantness, which are taken away by the evils of a most grievous slavery; and they are taken away for this reason, that she judged them given to her not by God, as to a wife, but by her lovers, as to a harlot, for the wages of lust. Then she will by no means have fruit-bearing trees, but everything will be turned into forest. And since he had once taken the metaphor from the woods, he carries it through in the rest, so as to call the enemies, by whom all things are to be devoured, beasts.

2:13.t: And I will visit upon her the days of the Baalim, on which she burned incense and adorned herself with her earring and her necklace, and went after her lovers, and forgot me, says the Lord. LXX: And I will avenge upon her the days of the Baalim, on which she sacrificed to them; and she put her earrings and necklaces about herself, and went after her lovers; but me she forgot, says the Lord. He keeps up the character of the harlot, who adorns herself with gold and gems to please her lovers, and whatever beauty she does not have by nature she procures by art. These earrings, with which her ears had been adorned by the teaching of God, and these pearls which hung precious from her neck, so that the bridegroom and husband said to her, Your neck is like necklaces, she cast before the feet of swine, and gave what is holy to the dogs. And what we read in Proverbs was fulfilled: Like a golden earring in a sow's nostrils, so is beauty to a most wicked woman. […]

2:14.t: For this reason God says of Jerusalem too: Behold, I will lead her astray, and I will make her like a desert, and set her like a land without water, and I will speak to her heart; and I will give her possessions from there, and the valley of Achor to open understanding (Hos 2:14, 15). Let us consider the order of each thing: he leads her astray, and makes her deserted and without water, so that she may suffer thirst for the virtues. After she has said, My soul has thirsted for you, how many ways my flesh for you (Ps 62 [63]:2), then he will speak to her heart and console her as she mourns. And he will give her a possession from there, that is, from the repentance and sorrow which works salvation. And the humility of her troubled heart (for this is what the valley of Achor means) opens her understanding, so that she may not be ignorant of her Creator.

Therefore, behold, I will allure her; and I will lead her into the wilderness, and I will speak to her heart. And I will give her her vinedressers from the same place, and the valley of Achor to open up hope. LXX: Therefore, behold, I will lead her astray and will make her like a desert; and I will speak to her heart and give her her possessions from there, and the valley of Achor to open up her understanding. Where we said to open up hope, and the LXX rendered to open up her understanding, Symmachus interpreted εἰς θύραν ἐλπίδος, that is, into a door of hope, Theodotion διανοῖξαι τὴν ὑπομονὴν αὐτῆς, that is, to open up her patience, or her expectation. […]

These things the circumcision and our own Judaizers refer to the reign of a thousand years, things which we see fulfilled in the beginning through the apostles as vinedressers and the many thousands of believers from Israel, and being fulfilled daily in those who are willing to believe. And where we said, I will allure her, and the LXX interpreted, I will lead her astray, they refer it to the time of the Antichrist, so that those who did not receive the truth of Christ may receive that one's lie, and afterwards, when Christ comes, may be saved.

2:15.t: And what follows: And I will give her her vinedressers from the same place. He who had set forth beforehand the caressing and the wilderness in the likeness of the past history of those who went out of Egypt, in which Moses and Aaron arose as princes from the same nation of the Jews, now too promises that he will give her vinedressers from the same place. That the vineyard is understood as Israel, all the scripture of both the Old and the New Testament bears witness: The vineyard of the Lord of Sabaoth is the house of Israel. And: You transferred a vineyard out of Egypt. And in the Gospel: The householder let out his vineyard and did not receive the fruits. And when his son had been killed, at the last he let it out to other vinedressers. This, then, is what the prophetic word promises: that the princes of this vineyard, going out from the nations and from the captivity of enemies, or of vices, should be of the very race of the Jews, that is, the apostles; […]

And she will sing there according to the days of her youth, and according to the days of her coming up from the land of Egypt. LXX: And she will be humbled according to the days of her infancy and according to the days of the coming up from the land of Egypt. In the place where we put she will sing, and the LXX translated she will be humbled, in the Hebrew is written anatha, which Symmachus interpreted 'she will be afflicted', Theodotion 'she will answer', Aquila 'she will obey', that is, ὑπακούσει; we take it rather from the Hebrew κατὰ λέξιν (word for word), that is, 'she will lead the singing'; so that, since he had once set down the being tossed about and the leading out into the wilderness, and the vinedressers from the same place, and the valley of Achor, touching in brief speech on the whole history of those who went out of Egypt and journeyed to the holy land, he might even now keep the likeness of the history. […]

2:16.t: And it will be on that day, says the Lord, she will call me My husband, and will no longer call me Baalim; and I will take away the names of the Baalim from her mouth, and she will no longer remember their name. LXX: likewise. That Ninus, the son of Belus, was the first to reign over all Asia, all histories, both Greek and barbarian, relate; he founded among the Assyrians the city of Ninus, named after himself, which the Hebrews call Nineveh. His wife Semiramis, of whom many marvelous things are told, built the walls of Babylon. Of her the famous poet bears witness, saying: "Where Semiramis is said once to have girded the city with walls of baked brick." He fought in a strong contest against the great Zoroaster, king of the Bactrians, and came to such glory that he enrolled his father Belus as a god; he is called Bel in Hebrew, and in many prophets, and above all in Daniel according to Theodotion, he is called by this name as the idol of Babylon. The Sidonians and Phoenicians call him Baal; […]

2:18.t: For He hath come as a Physician, not as a Judge. Therefore in like manner as those of old took harlots for wives, even so God too espoused unto Himself the nature which had played the harlot: and this also prophets from the beginning declare to have taken place with respect to the Synagogue. But that spouse was ungrateful towards Him who had been an husband to her, whereas, the Church, when once delivered from the evils received from our fathers, continued to embrace the Bridegroom.
2:18.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 3:5

2:18.t: And I will strike a covenant for them in that day with the beast of the field, and with the bird of the sky, and with the creeping thing of the earth; and the bow, and the sword, and war I will crush out of the land; and I will make them sleep confidently. LXX: And I will arrange a covenant for them in that day with the beasts of the field, and with the flying things of the sky, and with the creeping things of the earth; and the bow, and the sword, and war I will crush out of the land; and I will make them dwell in hope. When all the names of the hostile religion have been taken away from the people that confesses the Lord, and she calls me, he says, My husband, and by no means Baali, that is, my idol, then I will strike a covenant and concord for them with the beasts of the field, and the birds of the sky, and the creeping things of the earth. Of this time Isaiah also speaks: The wolf will dwell with the lamb; and the leopard will lie down with the kid. […]

2:19.t: Who would not grieve over such things and say, “How is the faithful city become an harlot?” How would not the Lord Himself say to some of those who are now walking in the spirit of Jeremiah, “Hast thou seen what the virgin of Israel has done to me?” I betrothed her to me in trust, in purity, in righteousness, in judgment, in pity, and in mercy; as I promised her through Hosea the prophet. But she loved strangers, and while I, her husband, was yet alive, she is called adulteress, and is not afraid to belong to another husband.

You have wisely thought it a subject of inquiry, whether there be any difference in God's love towards those who have believed from their childhood, and those who have believed in the course of their youth or more advanced age; for this also has not been past over nor left unnoticed in the sacred Scriptures. For it is not without meaning that the Lord our God says to the Prophet Joel, Lament to me for the spouse girded with sackcloth and for the husband of her youth, expressing his grief for the Synagogue, who, before, in her virginity, had been espoused to the Word of God, or, it may be, for a soul which had fallen from her good deeds, that by the heinousness of her sins she had incurred hatred, and through the defilement of impiety and the stains of unbelief had become miserable and despised, and far removed from the grace of that Spouse which had before been counted worthy to be told, I will betroth thee unto Me in righteousness and in judgment and in loving kindness and in mercies.

And I will betroth you to me for ever; and I will betroth you to me in justice and judgment, and in mercy and in compassions; and I will betroth you to me in faith, and you will know that I am the Lord. LXX: likewise. O how great is the clemency of God! The harlot who has played the harlot with many lovers, and for her crime was handed over to the beasts, after she returns to her husband, is by no means said to be reconciled to him, but to be betrothed. And see what difference there is between the union of God and that of men: a man, when he has taken a wife, makes a woman out of a virgin, that is, not a virgin; God, even when joined to harlots, changes them into virgins, according to that which is said to the adulteress through Jeremiah: You have not called upon me as lord, or father, or prince of your virginity. Hence the Apostle too speaks to the Corinthians who believed after fornication and the worship of idols: For I have betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. […]

2:21.t: And it will be in that day: I will hear, says the Lord, I will hear the heavens, and they will hear the earth, and the earth will hear the wheat and the wine and the oil, and these will hear Jezreel, and I will sow her for myself in the land, and I will have mercy on her who was Without Mercy; and I will say to Not My People: You are My People; and he will say: You are my God. LXX: And it will be in that day, says the Lord: I will hear the heaven, and the heaven will hear the earth, and the earth will hear the grain, the wine, and the oil, and these will hear Jezreel, and I will sow her for myself upon the land, and I will love her who was not loved; and I will say to Not My People: You are My People; and he will say: You are the Lord my God. In that day and at that time, when I have betrothed you to me in faith, and you have known that I am the Lord, I will hear the heavens, which tell the glory of God, and the heavens will hear the earth, so as to water it with heavenly rain; […]

Concerning the hearing of heaven and earth, and of the grain, wine and oil, and of Jezreel, some hold this view: that after Christ has come, all things will run in their own order, and the whole creation will serve the advantage of men, as it was founded in the beginning. All these things the Jews and our Judaizers await bodily, after the Antichrist, at the end of the world.

2:23.t: And not only is the operation of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit everywhere one but also there is one and the same will, calling, and giving of commands, which one may see in the great and saving mystery of the Church. For as the Father called the Gentiles to the Church, saying: "I will call her My people which was not My people, and her beloved who was not beloved;" and elsewhere: "My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations," so, too, the Lord Jesus said that Paul was chosen by Him to call forth and gather together the Church, as you find it said by the Lord Jesus to Ananias: "Go, for he is a chosen vessel unto Me to bear My name before all nations." As, then, God the Father called the Church, so, too, Christ called it, and so, too, the Spirit called it, saying: "Separate Me Paul and Barnabas for the work to which I have called them." "So," it is added, "having fasted and prayed, they laid hands on them and sent them forth. And they, being sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia." […]

Having then given to the question that answer which was furnished by facts, in order to give his discourse the advantage of other testimony in its favor, he introduces the prophets also making the same declarations aforetime. For Hosea, he says, of old put this in writing, as follows: "I will call them My people, which were not My people; and her beloved, which was not beloved." Here to prevent their saying, that you are deceiving us here with specious reasoning, he calls Hosea to witness, who crieth and saith, "I will call them My people, who were not My people." Who then are the not-people? Plainly, the Gentiles. And who the not-beloved? The same again. However, he says, that they shall become at once people, and beloved, and sons of God. "For even they shall be called," he says, "the children of the living God." But if they should assert that this was said of those of the Jews who believed, even then the argument stands. […]

And that harlot who had been joined to God, and had borne three children, two males and one female, the first Jezreel, the second Without Mercy, the third Not My People, may see that because of the seed of God the names of things have been changed, and that in the faith of Christ she who was Without Mercy has obtained mercy, and he who was formerly called Not a People has been called the people of God. From this we perceive that everything that has been said can be referred both to the ten tribes, which are called Israel, and which under the name of the harlot bore three children, and to the whole race of the Jewish name.

"You who were once not a people but now are the people of God, who did not seek after mercy but now have received mercy." By these verses he indicates clearly that he has written this letter to those who had come from the Gentiles to the faith, who were once separated from the way of life of the people of God but then through the grace of faith were joined to his people and obtained the mercy that they did not know how to hope for. He takes them, however, from the prophet Hosea, who predicted the calling of the Gentiles and said, "I shall call [those who were] not my people my people and [those who did] not receive mercy [a people] having received mercy. And it will be in the place where it was said, 'You are not my people,' there they will be called sons of the living God."
2:23.s: Commentary on the Catholic Epistles, 1 Peter 2:10

3:1.t: And the Lord said to me: Go again, love a woman loved by a friend and an adulteress, as the Lord loves the sons of Israel; and they look to other gods, and love the husks of grapes. LXX: And the Lord said to me: Go again and love a woman who loves evil things and an adulteress, as the Lord loves the sons of Israel; and they look to other gods, and love cooked cakes with grape-husks. To the former woman the prophet is joined as a type of the ten tribes, or of the whole Jewish people playing the harlot, and at length he received back into salvation the children who had been cast off and tormented; here he is ordered to love an adulterous woman again. When it is said: again, does it show that he had loved a fornicatress before, who as an adulteress either loves those evil things or is loved by a friend and neighbor? For the Hebrew word Re is read either as evil or as friend. […]

3:2.t: These then are that seven and eight whereof Hosea says that by that number he purchased to himself, and acquired the fulness of faith, for thus it is written, So I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and for an homer of barley, and an half homer of barley, and a measure of wine. But in the former verses God had commanded him to hire to himself an harlot, and it is manifest that he did so, in that he has mentioned the price of her hiring. Now the fifteen pieces of silver are made up of the numbers seven and eight, wherefore they represent these numbers.

And I dug her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver, and a cor of barley, and half a cor of barley, and I said to her: Many days you will wait for me; you will not play the harlot, and you will not be for a man; but I also will wait for you. LXX: And I hired her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver, and a gomor of barley, and a nebel of wine, and I said to her: Many days you will sit for me; and you will not play the harlot, nor will you be for another man, and I for you. For gomor, in the Hebrew is written omer, which all the translators, except the LXX, have rendered cor, a word Greek and especially Palestinian, which holds thirty modii. And for nebel of wine, in the Hebrew is read lethech seorim, which the other translators rendered ἡμίκορον of barley, that is, half a cor, which makes fifteen modii. And what is added in the common edition: Nor will you be for another man; another is not found in the Hebrew, but simply you will not be for a man. […]

3:4.t: I ask therefore on what day the manna began to be given from heaven, and I wish to compare our Lord's day with the sabbath of the Jews. For from the divine scriptures it appears that the manna was first given upon the earth on the Lord's day. For if, as Scripture says, it was gathered for six continuous days, but on the seventh day, which is the sabbath, there was a cessation, without doubt its beginning was from the first day, which is the Lord's day. But if from the divine scriptures this is established, that on the Lord's day God rained the manna and on the sabbath he did not rain it, let the Jews understand that even then our Lord's day was preferred to the Jewish sabbath, that even then it was indicated that on their sabbath no grace of God came down to them from heaven, that no heavenly bread, which is the word of God, came to them. […]

For many days the sons of Israel will sit without a king, and without a prince, and without sacrifice, and without altar, and without ephod, and without teraphim. And after this the sons of Israel will return and will seek the Lord their God and David their king; and they will tremble before the Lord and before his goodness in the last of days. LXX: For many days the sons of Israel will sit without a king, without a prince, without sacrifice, without altar, without priesthood, without manifestations, — which in Greek are called δῆλοι —. And after this the sons of Israel will return, and will seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and they will be astonished before the Lord, and at his good things on the last day. For ephod and teraphim the Seventy translated ἱερατείαν, that is, priesthood, and δήλους, that is, manifestations. […]

The present section some of the Jews interpret of the Babylonian captivity, when the temple was desolate for seventy years, and there were no altar and victims and priesthood, and afterwards under Zerubbabel they returned to their former seats. Others, like us, defer it to the future time; and what is the cause of so great an offense, that they have been abandoned for so long a time, especially since they do not worship idols, they cannot find any other than the killing of the Savior.

3:5.t: This is the blindness which has happened in part to Israel, so that the fullness of the Gentiles might come in, and then all Israel would be saved; and after a long time they will return and will seek the Lord their God, and David their king, who was born of the stock of David, and whose name is interpreted strong of hand. For he himself released the captivity of his people, and gave release to those in bonds. And when the sons of Israel see him, who was denied by his own brothers, reigning in the majesty of the Father and in his own, they will tremble and be astonished before the Lord and before his Good One, he who, a good son, was born of a good father; or to the good things of the Lord, of which the saint speaks: I believe I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living; for this land which we sinners inhabit is the land of the dead.

4:1.t: Hear the word of the Lord, sons of Israel, for the Lord has a judgment with the inhabitants of the earth. For there is no truth, and there is no mercy, and there is no knowledge of God on the earth; cursing, and lying, and murder, and theft, and adultery have flooded in; and blood has touched blood. LXX: Hear the word of the Lord, sons of Israel, for the Lord has a judgment against the inhabitants of the earth; for there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God upon the earth. Cursing, and lying, and murder, and theft, and adultery have been poured out upon the earth, and they have mingled blood with blood. From the beginning of the prophet up to this place, under the description of a harlot and of an adulteress, after whose most grievous punishments and very long abandonment there comes afterwards a restoration to the former, or to a better, state, the sins of the ten tribes, or of the two, and of all in common, are enumerated. […]

4:3.t: Because of this the earth will mourn, and everyone who dwells in it will languish; with the beast of the field and with the bird of the sky; and even the fish of the sea will be gathered up. LXX: Therefore the earth will mourn and will be diminished with all who inhabit it: with the beasts of the field, with the serpents of the earth, and with the fowls of the sky, and the fish of the sea will fail. Because there is no truth, and there is no mercy, and there is no knowledge of God upon the earth; but, over against these, cursing and lying, and murder and theft and adultery have flooded in, and blood has touched blood. Therefore the earth will mourn with its inhabitants, and will languish, so that it has no beasts of the field and birds of the sky, and the fish of the sea will fail. For when the captivity of the ten tribes has come, once the inhabitant has been taken away, the beasts too and the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea will fail, and even the mute elements will feel the wrath of the Lord. […]

4:4.t: Nevertheless let no one judge, and let no man be reproved; for your people are like those who contradict the priest; and you will fall today, and the prophet too will fall with you. LXX: So that no one is either judged, or anyone reproved; but my people are like a priest who will be contradicted, and he will be weakened by day, and the prophet too will be weakened with you. According to the Seventy translators, this which we have set down, so that no one is either judged, or anyone reproved, must be fitted to the preceding section. But let us follow the Hebrews. The sons of Israel who dwelt in the land, having been summoned to the judgment of God to hear the causes of the Lord's indignation and to recognize the past sins for which they were to be handed over to their enemies, now, because they persevere in their crimes and despise God with a shameless brow, hear: There is no need for you to come to judgment, to be reproved for your outrages; […]

4:5.t: And because you are such, therefore today you fall, that is, you are led into captivity, and you lose the kingdom of Israel. Now as for his saying: today, it either signifies the present time, or that you will be led into captivity not by fraud and ambush but in broad daylight; and so great will be your weakness that even the prophets, who used to prophesy a lie to you, will fall with you and experience captivity. Here we ought to understand by the prophets either the false prophets, or at least every prophetic grace. For as long as the ten tribes had not been taken captive, they had both the prophet Elijah and Elisha, and the other sons of the prophets, who prophesied in Samaria. Hence also the prophet Amos, who was of the tribe of Judah and of the little village of Tekoa, is compelled to return to his own country, so as not to prophesy in a foreign kingdom and in Samaria.

By night I have made your mother silent.

My people has fallen silent, because it had no knowledge; because you have rejected knowledge, I too will reject you, so that you may not serve as priest to me; and you have forgotten the law of your God, I too will forget your sons. LXX: I have likened your mother to the night, and my people has been likened to one not having knowledge; because you have rejected knowledge, I too will reject you, so that you may not serve as priest to me; you have forgotten the law of your God, and I too will forget your sons. He calls them mother and sons, not because the mother is one thing and the sons another; but just as the Lord, speaking to the people of the Jews, said: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you, how often I wished to gather your sons, as a hen gathered her chicks under her wings, and you would not? Not that Jerusalem was one thing and her people another; […]

For He even said by one of the holy prophets to the people of the Jews, "I have compared your mother to the night: My people is like to him that has no knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being My priest: and because you have forgotten the law of your God, I will also forget your sons." Observe therefore that He compares Jerusalem to the night; for the darkness of ignorance veiled the heart of the Jews, and blinded their eyes: and for this reason they were given over to destruction and slaughter.
4:5.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

4:6.t: Because the ecclesiastical hierarchy is founded upon Scripture, which is compared to the water of the sea, therefore sentence has been passed against those who do not possess this knowledge. In Hosea: "Because you have rejected knowledge, I will reject you, that you shall not minister to me as priest." He who knows nothing of governance is driven from the helm of the ship and from the rule of the city. If the foundations of the Church consist in the knowledge of sacred Scripture, therefore he who does not know sacred Scripture must be driven from ecclesiastical office and dignity. If a blind man wished to lead another, it would be the greatest folly. A helmsman is not to be chosen by lot or by friendship. And it should be known that knowledge is rejected when a man does not take care to learn it.

4:7.t: According to their multitude, so have they sinned against me; I will change their glory into disgrace, and they will eat the sins of my people, and will lift up their souls to their iniquities; and it will be, as the people, so the priest; and I will visit upon him his ways, and I will repay him his thoughts. LXX: According to their multitude, so have they sinned against me; I will turn their glory into disgrace; they will eat the sins of my people, and in their iniquities they will take their souls, and it will be, as the people, so also the priest; and I will avenge upon him his ways, and I will repay him his thoughts. As many men as Israel had, so many altars did it build to demons, in whose victims it sinned against me. Therefore their glory, in which they gloried for themselves and preferred idols to God, I will change into disgrace, so that both priests and peoples are taken captive.

Concerning the heretics the understanding is easy: that the more numerous they are, the more they sin against God and glory in their peoples; and therefore they deceive the unhappy, so as to eat the sins of the people, and through sweet words to devour the houses of widows. For when they see some people sinning, they say: God seeks nothing else but the truth of faith; if you guard it, he does not care what you do. For by saying these things they lift up their souls in their iniquities, so that they not only do not repent nor are humbled, but rejoice in their crimes and walk with neck held high. Hence both the people and the priest, both those who have been taught and those who taught, will be bound by an equal judgment.

4:8.t: For indeed the priests eat the sins of my people, the priests of whom it is written: Who devour my people as a meal of bread. And they eat the sins of my people for this reason, that they consent to the crimes of those who offend; for when they have seen them sinning, they not only do not reprove them, but praise and extol them, and proclaim them blessed. Of these Isaiah too speaks: My people, those who call you blessed lead you astray, and trip up the paths of your feet. Of these the psalmist also cries out: For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul, and the unjust man is blessed.

But we must remember without ceasing what is written about certain ones: They shall eat the sins of my people. Why are they said to eat the sins of the people, unless because they encourage the sins of transgressors, lest they lose their temporal payments? But we also who live from the offerings of the faithful, which they offered for their sins, if we eat and remain silent, we without doubt eat their sins. Let us consider, therefore, what a crime it is before God to eat the price of sins and to do nothing against sins by preaching.

4:9.t: Hence the people and the priest alike will bear the sentence of an indignant God; because he will visit not only their works, which are called ways, in which they walk, but also the thoughts with which they deliberated in order to do such things. For not only the work, but also the thought of an evil work will pay the penalty.

We seek no gain of souls, we attend daily to our own pursuits, we desire earthly things, we eagerly chase human glory with intent mind. And because by the very fact that we are placed over others, we have greater license to do whatever we wish, we turn the ministry of the blessing we received into an instrument of ambition; we abandon God's cause, we attend to earthly business; we receive a place of holiness, and we are entangled in earthly activities. What is written has surely been fulfilled in us: "And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest." For the priest does not differ from the people when by no merit of his own does he transcend the common conduct.

4:10.t: And they will eat and will not be satisfied; they have played the harlot and have not ceased, since they have forsaken the Lord in not observing; fornication and wine and drunkenness take away the heart. My people has inquired of its wood, and its staff has declared to it. For the spirit of fornications deceives them, and they have played the harlot away from their God. LXX: And they will eat and will not be filled; they have played the harlot and will not be set straight, because they have forsaken the Lord, so as not to observe; the heart of my people has taken up fornication and wine and drunkenness; they inquired by auguries, and by their rods they made announcement to it; for they have been led astray by a spirit of fornication and have played the harlot away from their God. Pleasure is insatiable, and the more of it is taken, the more hunger it creates in those who use it. On the contrary, blessed are those who hunger and thirst for justice, for they shall be satisfied. […]

The ten tribes too played the harlot with the idols of Jeroboam son of Nebat; and they forsook their God, not keeping what he had commanded when he said: You shall worship the Lord your God and serve him alone, but this is to be read ἐμφατικῶς (emphatically): Fornication and wine and drunkenness take away the heart. For just as wine and drunkenness make him who has drunk no longer master of his mind, so fornication and pleasure pervert the sense and weaken the spirit, and make of a rational man a brute animal, so that he pursues eating-houses and brothels and the dens of lusts. And when the heart has thus been moved from its place, it thinks wood and stones are gods and worships the works of its own hands.

The heretics are never satisfied with their error, nor do they cease from the foulness of fornication, and daily, by not keeping the law and the holy Scriptures, they forsake the Lord, they rave and become drunk; and having lost the judgment of the mind, they worship idols which they have fashioned from their own heart, and are possessed by the spirit of fornication.

4:12.t: Hence the prophet too, as if astonished and full of wonder, declares: My people, which was once called by my name, has inquired of wood and of rods; a kind of divination which the Greeks call ῥαβδομαντείαν (divination by rods). Hence we also read in Ezekiel that Nebuchadnezzar mixed his rods against Ammon and Jerusalem, and the rod came out against Jerusalem; and the cause of this madness is the spirit of fornication, which deceived them, so that they played the harlot away from their God. Now fornication signifies idolatry, according to what we read in Jeremiah: And they committed adultery with wood and stone, and I said: After they have played the harlot with all these, return to me; and she did not return with her whole heart, but in falsehood. And again: You have forsaken me and said: I will go upon every high hill, and I will pour myself out in my fornication under every leafy tree. And in the psalm it is said: You have destroyed all who play the harlot away from you. […]

4:13.t: On the tops of the mountains they sacrificed, and on the hills they burned incense; under the oak and the poplar and the terebinth, because its shade was good. LXX: On the summit of the mountains they sacrificed, and on the hills they offered victims; under the oak and the poplar and the shady trees, because the shelter was good. In the law it is commanded that no sacrifice be made to the Lord except in the place which the Lord God shall choose; and that a grove and trees not be planted beside the altar, lest, namely, a promiscuous and pleasure-loving religion overturn the austerity of the one and true religion. On the contrary, Israel sacrificed on the mountains and burned incense on the hills, loving the high places of the earth because it had forsaken God on high, and seeking the shade it had lost the truth. This is what we read of the several kings: Nevertheless he did not take away the high places; the people still offered victims and sacrificed on the high places, which in Hebrew is called bama. […]

It is a grave displeasure, after you have sinned, not to merit the wrath of the Lord. Israel had played the harlot away from the Lord his God and been led astray by a spirit of fornication; therefore his daughters and brides also play the harlot and are left in their crime without any punishment, so that what the sons and the wife had done to their true parent and husband, they may feel in their own children and wives, and from their own pain understand the pain of God, who is so angry that he does not strike the offenders at all. The Apostle too, writing to the Romans, testifies to this in mystical speech: For, saying that they were wise, they became fools; and they changed the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of the image of corruptible man, and of birds, and of four-footed beasts, and of serpents. […]

4:14.t: But do you wish to hear the terrible voice of an indignant God? Hear what he says through the prophet: when he had enumerated the many wicked things which the people had committed, he adds also these: "and for this reason" he says "I will not visit upon your daughters when they fornicate, nor upon your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery". This is the terrible thing, this the extremity: when we are no longer rebuked for our sins, when we are no longer corrected when we transgress. For then, when we have exceeded the measure of sinning, the "jealous God" turns his jealousy away from us, as he said above: "for my jealousy shall be taken away from you, and I will be angry over you no more". So much concerning that which was said: "a jealous God".

Therefore your daughters will play the harlot, and your brides will be adulteresses.

I will not visit upon your daughters when they have played the harlot, and upon your brides when they have committed adultery; since they themselves consorted with harlots and sacrificed with the effeminate; and the people that does not understand will be beaten. LXX: Therefore your daughters will play the harlot and your brides will commit adultery, and I will not visit upon your daughters when they have played the harlot and upon your brides when they have committed adultery; because they themselves also mingled with harlots and offered victims with the initiated; and the people that understands clung to the harlot. The word cadesoth, which Aquila translated ἐνηλλαγμένων, Symmachus ἑταιρίδων, the Seventy τετελεσμένων, Theodotion κεχωρισμένων, we have rendered 'effeminate', so as to lay open the sense of the word to the ears of our own people. […]

4:15.t: If you play the harlot, Israel, let Judah at least not sin; and do not go into Gilgal; and do not go up to Beth-aven, nor swear: The Lord lives; for like a wanton cow Israel has turned aside. Now the Lord feeds them like a lamb in a broad place. LXX: But you, Israel, do not be ignorant, and Judah, do not go into Gilgal, do not go up to the house of ὢν, and do not swear: The Lord lives; for like a cow stung by the gadfly Israel has gone mad. Now the Lord feeds them like a lamb in a spacious place. For 'house of ὢν', in certain copies, and especially in Theodotion, 'house of iniquity' is read, which Aquila and Symmachus translated 'house of ἀνωφελοῦς', that is, useless, which profits nothing and by another word is called an idol. Now it is Bethel, which formerly was called house of God; after the calves were set up in it, it was called Beth-aven, that is, house of uselessness and house of the idol, which we have expressed as it is read in the Hebrew. […]

Concerning the heretics the understanding is ready at hand, to whom, or of whom, it is said: If once you play the harlot, heretic, at least you, churchman, do not sin, nor go into Gilgal, the conventicles of the heretics, where the sins of all are revealed, and like swine they wallow in the mire. Nor think that you are going up to the proud and arrogant fictions of false dogmas. For there is not the house of God, but the house of the idol. Nor swear by the name of Christ, whose majesty you have polluted by mingling it with idols. For like a cow stung by the gadfly, the heretics have been struck by the burning arrows of the devil and have abandoned the knowledge of the law; therefore they will be pastured on the broad and spacious way that leads to death, and the patience of the Lord, the good shepherd, will nourish them for destruction.

4:16.t: For as a wanton cow, casting off the yoke of the law, so Israel, that is, the ten tribes, has turned aside from the service of the Lord. For 'wanton cow' the Seventy translated παροιστρῶσαν, one stung by the oestrus and the asilus, which is commonly called the tabanus. Of this Vergil also tells in the third book of the Georgics: "whose Roman name is asilus, the Greeks turned it oestrus, so calling it; fierce, sounding harshly; terrified by it, whole herds scatter through the woods; the air, shaken, rages with bellowing, and the woods and the bank of dry Tanagrus". Since, therefore, Israel has gone mad and, struck by the spirit of fornication, has raved with incredible fury, therefore not long afterward, but while I prophesy, while breath rules these limbs, the Lord feeds them like a lamb in a broad place. […]

In another place, the prophet heapeth contumely upon Israel who had slipped his shoulder from [under] the yoke of the divine commandments: "As an ox which hath escaped from the yoke, so have the children of Israel escaped, they and their kings and their nobles." Now Israel became rebels because there was no fear [in them]; and they trod under foot the commandments because they were not mindful of what was threatened; and they despised the law because they remembered not the penalty of Him that ordained it.
4:16.s: 13 Ascetic Discourses, Discourse 6 -- First Discourse on the Fear of God

4:17.t: That which the Seventy set down: he has provoked the Canaanites, is not found in the Hebrew. Yet it can be interpreted thus, so that we say that Israel had such zeal in the worship of idols that he did not imitate the Canaanites, that is, the heathen, but provoked them to imitate his own error.

Ephraim is a partaker of idols; let him go; their banquet is set apart; in fornication they have played the harlot; his protectors loved to bring disgrace; the spirit has bound him in its wings; and they will be put to shame by their sacrifices. LXX: Ephraim, a partaker of idols, has set stumbling blocks for himself, he has provoked the Canaanites; playing the harlot they have played the harlot, they have loved disgrace from their roaring; you are a whirlwind of the spirit in its wings, and they will be put to shame by their altars. Ephraim, the tribe from which came Jeroboam son of Nebat, who first set up the golden calves in Bethel and Dan, is king of the ten tribes. O Judah, then, to whom I said above: If Israel plays the harlot, let Judah at least not sin, hear my counsel, do not spurn the words of the prophet: since Ephraim is once for all a friend and partaker of idols, let him go, lest you follow his impiety, whose worship and religion and food are set apart from your banquet. […]

This same thing can also be referred to the heretics, and it is said to Judah, that is, to the churchman: since Ephraim, which is interpreted καρποφόρος (fruit-bearing), promises himself a false richness of doctrine and fruitful dogmas, and is once for all a friend of demons, let him go and despise him, especially since their sacrifices are set apart from your sacrifices. For this is what he says: their banquet is set apart; they have played the harlot once for all, and their princes have deceived the unhappy people; and in place of the worship of God they have steeped them in the disgrace of idols, and the spirit of the devil has bound them in its wings, they who are carried about by every wind of doctrine and cannot remain with a steady foot in the Church. They truly will be put to shame in their sacrifices, because their bread is the bread of mourning. […]

5:1.t: Is the undertaking then so serious and laborious to a sensitive and sad heart—a very rottenness to the bones of a sensible man: while the danger is slight, and a fall not worth consideration? Nay the blessed Hosea inspires me with serious alarm, where he says that to us priests and rulers pertaineth the judgment, because we have been a snare to the watchtower; and as a net spread upon Tabor, which has been firmly fixed by the hunters of men's souls, and he threatens to cut off the wicked prophets, and devour their judges with fire, and to cease for a while from anointing a king and princes, because they ruled for themselves, and not by Him.

Hear this, O priests, and attend, house of Israel, and house of the king; listen with your ears, for the judgment is for you; since you have become a snare to the watchtower and a net spread over Tabor, and you have turned aside the victims into the depth. LXX: Hear this, O priests, and attend, house of Israel, and house of the king; perceive with your ears, for the judgment is against you, because you have become a snare to the watchtower; and like a net spread over Itabyrium, which those who take the prey have fixed fast for the hunt. The priests of the ten tribes are summoned to judgment, and the kings: not that the priests are of the tribe of Levi, but that they are called priests by the people. Hence too the priests of Baal, the four hundred and fifty prophets whom Elijah, and afterwards Jehu son of Nimshi in the presence of Jonadab son of Rechab, killed, were called priests; but Israel too, that is, the people, is summoned to judgment; […]

According to tropology, the people is accused so that it may not think itself free of the crime if it was led astray by kings and priests, whom we understand as the princes of the heretics. The princes themselves are also accused, because like a snare they caught the people and, though set as watchmen in the Church, led them into error. And on Mount Tabor, lofty and most beautiful, which is interpreted coming light, they laid ambushes, so as to drag all whom they had deceived down into the depth and sacrifice them to demons, and turn aside the victims into the abyss, lest they should ever come to their senses, lest they should look up to the Church, the house of God. Some think that Tabor is interpreted pit, that is, cistern; and that it fits the present sense that the heretics have dug a pit and fallen into the ditch which they made.
