There are some also who investigate spiritual precepts with cunning care, but what they penetrate with their understanding they trample on in their lives: all at once they teach the things which not by practice but by study they have learnt; and what in words they preach by their manners they impugn. Whence it comes to pass that when the shepherd walks through steep places, the flock follows to the precipice. Hence it is that the Lord through the prophet complains of the contemptible knowledge of shepherds, saying, "When ye yourselves had drunk most pure water, ye fouled the residue with your feet; and My sheep fed on that which had been trodden by your feet, and drank that which your feet had fouled." For indeed the shepherds drink most pure water, when with a right understanding they imbibe the streams of truth. But to foul the same water with their feet is to corrupt the studies of holy meditation by evil living. […]
5:1.s: The Book of Pastoral Rule, Part 1, Chapter 2

5:2.t: And the victims, he says, you have turned aside into the depth, so that no one should repent, nor the slain lift up his head. Both the kings and the priests prevented the people from going to the temple at Jerusalem; therefore they are said to have turned aside the victims into the depth.

And I am the instructor of them all.

I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me, for now Ephraim has played the harlot, Israel is defiled; they will not give their thoughts to return to their God, for the spirit of fornications is in their midst, and they have not known the Lord. LXX: For I am your teacher. I have known Ephraim, and Israel has not departed from me, for now Ephraim has played the harlot, Israel is stained; they have not given their thoughts to return to the Lord their God, for the spirit of fornication is in them. But the Lord they have not known. O priests and kings, who have deceived my people; and you, O people, who have been deceived: you have sinned so grievously that you have not only slain the victims, but have sent them into the depth of hell. Do not think that by the greatness of your crime you have departed wholly from me. I am your teacher, or rather your instructor, who desire to amend, not to punish; and to save, not to destroy.

5:3.t: I, he says, know Ephraim, that is, Jeroboam, by whom the people was seduced, and all the kings who followed him both in rank and in crime; and Israel is not hidden from me, that is, the people of the ten tribes, because when the king played the harlot, Israel was defiled. The king first began to play the harlot away from the worship of God, desiring to adore golden calves, and the people willingly followed, and they accomplished an equal impiety with equal zeal.

Hence the Lord is not ignorant of the princes of perverse dogmas, nor of the people; not that they are worthy of his knowledge, but that nothing escapes him of what they do in secret, of whom some have deceived and others have been deceived. Nor will they give their thoughts to repent, they who are always advancing in perdition. For the spirit of fornication with which they played the harlot in the Church and departed from the true marriage moves in their midst; therefore they have not known the Lord.

5:4.t: Finally, they will not return to the Lord, because what they wanted they have found, and the spirit of fornication, which according to the Apostle works in the sons of unbelief, possesses their captive hearts; therefore, while he reigned, they did not know the Lord, or rather they forgot their Creator.

5:5.t: And the arrogance of Israel will answer in his face; and Israel and Ephraim will fall in their iniquity, Judah also will fall with them. LXX: And the injury of Israel will be humbled into his face; and Israel and Ephraim will be weakened in their iniquities, Judah also will be weakened with them. The word gaon the Seventy and Symmachus translate as injury, Aquila and Theodotion as pride. Whatever, therefore, Israel has done, whether acting proudly against the Lord or venerating idols to the injury of the Creator, will answer in his face, so that he may not go away unpunished, but that his insolence may be humbled; and that the people and the kings may fall together in their iniquity, or be weakened, so that those who were strong in crime may be compelled, now weak, to return to the Lord. And this will befall not only Israel and Ephraim, that is, the ten tribes and their kings, so that they are led into captivity; […]

5:6.t: With their flocks and with their herds they will go to seek the Lord and will not find; he has been taken away from them; they have transgressed against the Lord, for they have begotten strange sons; now a month will devour them with their portions. LXX: With sheep and calves they will go to seek the Lord and will not find him; he has turned aside from them, because they have forsaken the Lord; because they have begotten strange sons for themselves, now rust will devour them, and their lots. Not only Israel and Ephraim will go with flocks and herds to seek the Lord, but Judah also, of whom it is written above: Judah also will fall with them; all of them having this one contest, that they strive to appease with victims him whom they have offended by their transgressions; and they do not find him whom they seek, because he too has departed from those who depart from him. Especially since he says elsewhere also: Shall I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats? […]

The heretics suppose that they appease God by a multitude of sacrifices; and churchmen, that by alms they redeem the sins in which they persist; whereas every sacrifice blots out past crimes, not present ones; therefore they do not find the Lord, who is taken away from such men and withdraws far off. These, indeed, have transgressed against God, and have begotten strange sons not to Christ but to the devil; therefore at all times their works are accursed, and all that they do the rust of bloody color lays waste, because they are next to blood and slaughter. Now rust is properly said to come down in the night dew and to stain the grain, still milky in the ear, with the color of vermilion or of red ochre; and fittingly, according to the ἀναγωγήν (anagogy), it lays waste the lots of the heretics, of whom it is said: Their lots will not profit them.

5:7.t: For they have transgressed against the Lord, because, playing the harlot with idols, they have begotten sons not to God but to demons. Others think that what is meant here is what is said in Ezra, a long time afterwards, when they took foreign wives, begetting children from them, and afterwards were compelled to put them away. But here it is better to take as strange sons those who were begotten in the error of idols, or those whom they led through the fire and consecrated to idols. Since, therefore, they have done this, not long afterwards, not after endless spans of years, nor, as I was formerly accustomed, foretelling things to come long after, but now and at this present time the Assyrian and the Chaldean will come; and they will devour them with their portions, or lots, that is, with the possessions which they received in the division of the land by the measure of the line. Where we said: a month will devour them, the Seventy translated rust; […]

5:8.t: Blow the horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah; howl in Beth-aven, behind your back, Benjamin; Ephraim will be in desolation in the day of rebuke; among the tribes of Israel I have shown faithfulness. LXX: Blow the trumpet upon the hills, sound upon the high places, proclaim in the house of ὤν; Benjamin has fallen out of his mind, Ephraim has become a desolation in the days of rebuke; among the tribes of Israel I have shown faithful things. The months one by one, or the rust, will devour Ephraim and Israel and Judah with their portions. Therefore I command you who hear to sound not with a loud voice but with a clear horn; for clear hearing is needed, so that all who are round about may hear. Blow the horn in Gibeah, whose etymology the Seventy translated as hills; and the trumpet in Ramah, which is interpreted high places; […]

Where we translated behind your back, Benjamin, the Seventy rendered Benjamin has been moved in mind, always fitting ἔκστασιν, that is, ecstasy of mind, to Benjamin, the churchman. Hence also in the sixty-seventh (68th) psalm it is said: There is Benjamin, a youth, in ecstasy of mind. And in the blessings of Jacob, under the person of Benjamin, of which tribe the apostle Paul was, we read it written: Benjamin is a ravening wolf; in the morning he will eat the prey, and at evening he will give food. For he who in the beginning persecuted the Church afterwards bestowed the nourishment of the Gospel on believers throughout the whole world. Hence also Saul, who was of the tribe of Benjamin, prophesied in ecstasy of mind all day until evening among the band of the prophets.

Some, following the Seventy, who said house of ὢν, have interpreted Beth-aven as the city of the sun; and, calling Christ the sun of justice, they would have his city be the Church. This displeases me; for the house of the idol, which Aquila translated useless house, cannot be referred to the Church even according to tropology. But let us say this: that the heretics, who in Gibeah and Ramah promise themselves lofty knowledge, are bidden to howl in the house of the idol, and are not before the face of Benjamin, which is interpreted son of the right hand, but behind his back, where he has no eyes. For all the boasting of Ephraim, which is interpreted fruitfulness, will shortly be in desolation; and when the day of judgment, he says, and the time of rebuke has come, I will show by deeds that my words are not empty.

5:9.t: For this reason, then, I say and command: Blow the horn in Gibeah, and the trumpet in Ramah, and howl in Beth-aven, because the royal house of Ephraim, or Ephraim himself, that is, the dominion of Israel, will now be in desolation, and captivity is close at hand. In the day of the rebuke and punishment of the ten tribes of Israel I have shown my words to be faithful, the words I threatened through the prophets, so that what I had foretold in word I might prove in deed.

5:10.t: The princes of Judah have become like those who take up the boundary; upon them I will pour out my wrath like water. LXX: The princes of Judah have become like those who move boundaries; upon them I will pour out my onrush like water. When Ephraim and Israel had been led into captivity and their land reduced to a wilderness, the princes of Judah, who ought to have wept, and to have exhorted their own people to withdraw from idolatry lest they too should suffer the like, began to rejoice and be glad that the land of those tribes lay open to them to possess more widely; and they became like those who take up the boundaries of Israel, passing beyond their own borders and desiring to extend their kingdom and possession into the places that once were Israel's. Therefore the Lord says: Upon these very princes of Judah too the Babylonians will come, and will thus overwhelm them like an onrush of water, not by their own strength but by my indignation. […]

5:11.t: Ephraim suffering wrong, broken in judgment, because he began to go after filth. LXX: Ephraim has oppressed his adversary, has trampled on judgment, because he began to go after vain things. If Ephraim is impious, and on account of his impiety will be in desolation, how is it now said: Ephraim suffering wrong, broken in judgment? For he who suffers wrong and is broken has his judgment unjustly overborne, all the more since a just cause is set down why he was handed over to captivity. For there follows: because he began to go after filth, that is, after idols, which are compared to filth. What he says, then, is this: Ephraim is oppressed by the Assyrians, first by Pul, then by Tiglath-pileser, afterwards by Shalmaneser; not that those who oppressed him were just, and that he was therefore handed over to them, but that those who were once my people, since I abandon them, are handed over to punishment; […]

5:12.t: And I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like rottenness to the house of Judah. LXX: And I am like a disturbance to Ephraim, and like a goad to the house of Judah. In the Hebrew language a moth is called As; recob is rottenness and decay; of which the one consumes garments, the other wood; for which the LXX translated ταραχὴν, that is, tumult or disturbance, and goad. And it must be noted that the moth is referred to Ephraim, and rottenness to the house of Judah. Just as, therefore, the moth consumes garments, and rottenness or decay consumes wood (both of which happen over a long time), so God, giving the ten tribes, and afterwards the two, room for repentance over a long time, and calling them to salvation, while they treasure up for themselves wrath in the day of wrath, becomes as it were a moth and rottenness; not that God is a moth or rottenness, or a disturbance or a goad, but that to those who suffer punishment all these things seem so. […]

5:13.t: And Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah his bond; and Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to the avenging king; and he will not be able to heal you, nor will he be able to loose the bond from you. LXX: And Ephraim saw his infirmity, and Judah his pain, and Ephraim went to the Assyrians, and sent envoys to King Jareb; and he will not be able to free you, nor will he make the pain cease from you. "Envoys" is not found in the Hebrew. And where the Seventy put Jareb, we, following Symmachus, have translated "avenger"; for Aquila and Theodotion rendered "judge". That Jareb signifies avenger and judge, the name of Gideon shows: when the worshipers of Baal demanded him for punishment, because he had overthrown the grove and the altars of Baal, his father answered: Let Baal avenge himself, or let Baal judge him; and he was called, it says, Jerubbaal, that is: let Baal avenge himself. […]

5:14.t: For I am like a lioness to Ephraim, and like a lion's whelp to the house of Judah. I, I will seize and go; I will carry off, and there is none who may rescue. Going, I will return to my place, until you fail and seek my face. LXX: For I am like a panther to Ephraim, and like a lion in the house of Judah. And I will snatch, and go, and carry off, and there will be none who may rescue; I will go and return to my place, until they perish and seek my face. While they go to Assyria and send to the vindicating or avenging king, who will not be able to heal them nor to loose the bond that binds them, I will show that, when I oppose, all the help of men is vain; for I will be like a lioness to Ephraim, and like a lion's whelp to the house of Judah. For lioness, which in Hebrew is called sohel, the Seventy rendered panther, which is said alike in Greek and in Latin, and can be taken both as the name of a beast and as "every beast"; so that whatever is savage in beasts you may recognize in the indignation of God. […]

To the heretics too, and to a negligent Church, God is turned into a panther and a lion; and he will take from them the prey which they formerly snatched from the Church, so that those who had perished while free may be saved by being captured; and he will by no means dwell in the conventicles of the perverse, but will return to his place, of which he says: I am in the Father and the Father in me, and he will spurn and despise them, until they fail in their impiety and seek through repentance him by whom they had been abandoned. Others think that the place of God is heaven, to which God, offended by those who dwell on earth, returns, and will make them perish who, by the greatness of their sins, have turned the most merciful Lord into the rage of wild beasts against themselves.

5:15.t: And as for what follows: Going, I will return to my place, by the place of God we ought to understand his magnificence and majesty; so that he no longer, by way of dispensation, descends to men, is angry, has mercy, forgets, becomes like a panther, is turned into a lion, is changed into beasts; but disregards human affairs and allows those whom he formerly protected to be subjected to their enemies, so that they may waste away, and fail, and perish, and afterwards seek the face of the Lord, and say: Make your face shine, and we shall be saved. And: Show us, O Lord, your mercy, and grant us your salvation.

In their tribulation they will rise early to me: come, and let us return to the Lord, for he has seized and he will heal us; he will strike and he will cure us; he will make us live after two days; on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight; we shall know and we shall follow, that we may know the Lord. LXX: In their tribulation they will watch early for me, saying: let us go and return to the Lord our God, for he will scourge and he will heal us; he will strike and he will cure us; he will make us whole after two days; on the third we shall rise again and we shall live before him and we shall know; let us pursue, that we may know the Lord. Therefore God has handed Ephraim and Judah over to captivity, and there is none who can snatch from his hand, and he will return to his place until they fail; and they will seek his face, so that him whom they had not felt as gracious and present, they may seek again as angry and absent; […]

6:1.t: The Holy Spirit set this forth of old, when he said in the Psalms, "O my king and my God. For to you will I pray; O Lord, in the morning you shall hear my voice. In the morning I will stand before you, and will see you." And again through the prophet the Lord says, "At dawn they will be on watch for me, saying, 'Let us go and return to the Lord our God.' " Likewise at the setting of the sun and at the end of the day necessarily there must again be prayer. For since Christ is the true sun and the true day, as the sun and the day of the world recede, when we pray and petition that the light come upon us again, we pray for the coming of Christ to provide us with the grace of eternal light.
6:1.s: Treatise IV. On the Lord's Prayer 35

6:1.t:
For to the beautiful promise to the righteous "though he fall, he shall not be utterly broken," has been added one more recent, "though he be utterly broken, he shall speedily be raised up and glorified." For if her misfortune was unreasonable, her recovery was extraordinary, so that health soon stole away the injury, and the cure became more celebrated than the blow.

O remarkable and wonderful disaster! O injury more noble than security! O prophecy, "He hath smitten, and He will bind us up, and revive us, and after three days He will raise us up," portending indeed, as it did, a greater and more sublime event, yet no less applicable to Gorgonia's sufferings!

And when they have risen early to the Lord, what will they say? Come, and let us return to the Lord. They are not content with their own salvation, but urge one another on to return to the Lord whom they had left, whom they had deserted because of their sins, by whom they had been abandoned. For he has seized and he will heal us; he who had said above: I, I will seize and go, will strike and heal us. For what we have said, "he will cure", all alike translated μοτώσει (will dress with lint); now properly μότα is the name for the little linen pads that are inserted into wounds, to eat away the putrid flesh and draw out the pus; and it belongs to the art of physicians to heal great wounds over a long time and to restore health through pain.

6:2.t: For hear what the prophet says: "God will raise us up after two days, and on the third day we shall rise again and shall live in his sight." The first day for us is the passion of the Savior, and the second, on which he descended into hell, but the third is the day of the resurrection. And therefore on the third day "God went before them, by day in a pillar of cloud, by night in a pillar of fire." But if, according to those things which we said above, the Apostle rightly teaches us that the mysteries of baptism are contained in these words, it is necessary that "those who are baptized in Christ should be baptized in his death, and be buried together with him," and rise again with him on the third day from the dead, whom also, according to that which the Apostle says: "he raised up together with himself, and made to sit together in the heavenly places." When, therefore, the mystery of the third day has been received by you, God will begin to lead you forth and Himself to show you the way of salvation.

And that he rose again on the third day according to the Scriptures. All things are enclosed in faith; therefore the resurrection of the Lord that was to take place on the third day was described in the person of the people. For Hosea the prophet says: After two days he will heal us, and on the third day we shall rise, and we shall live in his sight (Hos. 6:3). For none of the faithful denies that in Christ all have risen, just as in Adam all have died. In a similar way, in a psalm, under the person of man, he signifies Christ as well, saying: You have subjected all things under his feet: you have crowned him with glory and honor (Ps. 8:8).

The Lord therefore strikes and cures us; for whom the Lord loves he rebukes, and he chastises every son whom he receives; not only does he cure, but he makes alive after two days, and on the third day, rising again from hell, he raises up with himself the whole race of men. And when he has cured those who were struck, and made alive those who were cured, and raised up those who were made alive, then we shall live in his sight, we who, while he was absent, lay dead. And we shall live in his sight; we shall know him and follow him with all zeal, that we may know the Lord, by whose rising on the third day we have risen. By these words is explained what we have often already pointed out, that both Israel and Judah, that is, the ten and the two tribes, will then have one shepherd, and David as king, when they have believed in the Lord who rises again; […]

This is Hosea, the first of the twelve prophets who was privileged to speak concerning the Lord Christ in these terms: When they are afflicted, let them rise early to seek me saying, Come and let us return unto the Lord our God, for he hath smitten us and he will heal us; he that hath struck us will bind us up. After two days will he heal us. On the third day we shall be raised up again and we shall live! With reference to this passage the Apostle Paul says to the Corinthians: For I delivered unto you first of all that which also I received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures. For that he was buried, and that he was raised up on the third day according to the scriptures, is not to be found anywhere else.

6:3.t: Those who are thus continually engaged, are waiting entirely on the Lord, and say, ‘Let us follow on to know the Lord: we shall find Him ready as the morning, and He will come to us as the early and the latter rain for the earth.’ For not only does He satisfy them in the morning; neither does He give them only as much to drink as they ask; but He gives them abundantly according to the multitude of His lovingkindness, vouchsafing to them at all times the grace of the Spirit.

His going forth is prepared like the dawn, and he will come to us like the early rain, and the late rain to the earth. LXX: We shall find him prepared like the morning, and he will come to us like the early and the late rain to the earth. Come, he says, and let us return to the Lord, for he who has seized also will heal us, will strike and cure us, and will make us live after two days, and on the third day will raise us up; he himself and no other is prepared for us like the morning and the dawn. Of whom too is the title of the twenty-first (22nd) psalm: For the morning taking up; although in the Hebrew it is written: For the morning hart, because, having slain death and the twisting and ancient serpent, he longs to climb to the mountains; and he himself, the darkness scattered, rises for us as the sun of justice, to illuminate our blindness. And beautifully he says: his going forth is prepared. […]

6:4.t: What shall I do to you, Ephraim? What shall I do to you, Judah? Your mercy is like a morning cloud, and like the dew passing away in the morning; for this reason I have hewn them by the prophets, I have slain them by the words of my mouth, and your judgments will go forth like the light. LXX: What shall I do to you, Ephraim? What shall I do to you, Judah? But your mercy is like a morning cloud, and like the dew passing away in the morning; therefore I have cut down your prophets, I have slain them by the words of my mouth, and your judgment will go forth like the light. When he says: What shall I do to you, Ephraim? What shall I do to you, Judah? he shows the affection of a parent toward lost sons. According to what we read in Isaiah: What is there that I ought to have done further for my vineyard, and have not done for it? And in Micah: My people, what have I done to you, and in what have I been troublesome to you? […]

We perceive these same things to have been said also to the heretics, and to the true Judah, who is to suffer the like: that the Lord calls them to mercy and desires that they return to salvation. But they pursue the delights and refreshments of this age, like a cloud and dew that quickly passes away; to whom it is said in the Gospel: Fool, this night they require your soul of you; and the things you have prepared, whose will they be? And that rich man clothed in purple, who despised Lazarus lying before his gates, learned that all he had enjoyed had passed away like a cloud and dew. But God always slays the prophets of the heretics, when he threatens them with eternal punishments, and takes them away from the true life, and leaves them to the death of their crimes. But let us love that cloud which is everlasting, and which protects us from the heat of this world, sitting upon which the Lord came into Egypt and broke all the images of the Egyptians. […]

6:5.t: For already captivity is near, already I see you led in chains to the Assyrians and the Babylonians; I have hewn you by the prophets and threatened you with terrible words, I have brought out the scalpel, fire and cautery; so that you who despised me when I was merciful might fear me when offended; and I have slain the negligent by the words of my mouth, so that I might punish sinners by the terror of words before captivity was at hand. And all these things I have done so that the truth of the judgment with which I am about to judge you might appear, and no one might doubt that you have justly suffered what you suffer. For what is I have hewn them by the prophets, the Seventy translated: I have cut down your prophets, understanding the false prophets themselves to have been slain by the Lord; so that those who had been the cause of error, by promising prosperity, might, when slain, be turned into an occasion of salvation. And the sense is: Lest you should say: We believed the prophets; […]

6:6.t: For to every one who has turned to God in truth and with a whole heart, the doors are open, and the thrice-glad Father receives his truly repentant child. And true repentance is to be no longer bound in the same sins for which he denounced death against himself, but to eradicate them completely from the soul. For on their uprooting God takes up his abode again in you. For it is said there is great and exceeding joy and festivity in the heavens with the Father and the angels when one sinner turns and repents. This is why he cries, "I will have mercy, and not sacrifice."
6:6.s: Who is the Rich Man that Shall Be Saved?

6:6.t: For the Word of God Himself tells us that He prefers the performance of His commandments to the offering of sacrifice. God proclaims this, Moses declares it to the people, Paul preaches it to the Gentiles. Do that which you understand is most profitable for the time. "I prefer mercy," it is said, "rather than sacrifice." Are they not, then, rather Christians in truth who condemn their own sin, than they who think to defend it? "The just is an accuser of himself in the beginning of his words." He who accuses himself when he has sinned is just, not he who praises himself.

For I desired mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings; but they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant; there they have dealt treacherously against me. LXX: For I desire mercy and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings; but they are like a man passing over the covenant. What follows in the Seventy: There Gilead despised me, a city that works vain things, and the rest, must be fitted to the following section; let us discuss what we have set down: I have hewn them by the prophets, I have slain them by the words of my mouth, I have threatened grievous things, so that I might have mercy on the penitent, so that I might stretch out my hand to those who have fallen and are rising. For I do not delight in sacrifices and victims, and in a multitude of burnt offerings. My victims and burnt offerings are the salvation of those who believe, the conversion of sinners.

Daily God calls to repentance both those who are outside the Church and those who sin while dwelling in the Church, and says to them: I desire mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. But they offer sacrilegious bread, and give alms, and appear to pursue humility; these, then, if they are truly done, I interpret as burnt offerings. But since they have abandoned the knowledge of God, in vain, with the head of faith cut off, do they boast that they have the other members; for they have transgressed the covenant of God in the Church, just as Adam transgressed in paradise; and they show themselves imitators of their ancient parent, so that, as he was cast out of paradise, so these too may be cast out of the Church.

But God said, I require mercy, and not sacrifice: and the acknowledgment of God, and not whole burnt offerings.

What is meant by mercy? and what by sacrifice? By mercy then is signified, Justification and grace in Christ: even that which is by faith. For we have been justified, not by the works of the law that we have done, but by His great mercy. And sacrifice means the law of Moses.
6:6.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

6:6.t: Counsel disposes to mercy: for there is nothing God counsels more in Scripture than to show mercy, which he esteems above all holocausts.

A man sees the slaughter of bodies, he grieves greatly. He therefore who sees the slaughter of souls, how can he restrain himself from tears? This grief is greatly pleasing to God. The Lord says concerning this knowledge: "I desire mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than holocausts." I know the infirmities of others: I ought to suffer with them.

6:7.t: But they have imitated Adam, so that what he had done in paradise, passing over my covenant and law, these did on earth. And there, that is, in paradise, all have dealt treacherously against me, in the likeness of the transgression of Adam. For it is no wonder if what went before in the parent is condemned in the children also.

6:8.t: Gilead, a city of those who work an idol, supplanted by blood, and like the jaws of robber men (or: of a robber; for it can be read either way). LXX: There Gilead despised me, a city that works vain things, and troubles the water, and your strength is that of a pirate man. We read that in Ramoth-gilead Jehu was anointed king, he who mingled blood with blood, and overthrew the house of Ahab, and before sunrise ordered heaps of the heads of his sons to be set up; in this city across the Jordan, in the possession of the tribe of Gad, an idol was consecrated; it was inhabited by priests, for it too was a city of fugitives. Therefore, the more celebrated it was and the greater its authority, because it had been assigned as the portion of the priests, so much the more was it, for Israel dwelling across the Jordan, the beginning of idolatry and of all evils, so that those who had sinned first were the first to be taken captive by the Assyrians. […]

6:9.t: A partner of the priests who kill on the way those going from Shechem, because they have wrought wickedness. LXX: The priests hid the way of the Lord, they killed Shechem, because they wrought iniquity. Symmachus translated this passage thus: The fellowship of the priests on the way were killing Shechem. Theodotion in this way: The priests hid the way, they were killing on the back. Aquila: The partnership of the priests on the way were slaying shoulders; and when we sought their meaning according to the history from a Hebrew, it was explained to us thus: The priests of Bethel, or rather the fanatics of Beth-aven, at the times of Passover and Pentecost and Tabernacles, when one had to go through Shechem, which today is called Neapolis, to Jerusalem, where alone it was lawful to sacrifice victims, used to post robbers along the road to lie in wait for those going, so that they might worship the golden calves in Dan and in Beth-aven rather than God in Jerusalem and in the temple. […]

6:10.t: In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing; there Israel has been defiled by the fornication of Ephraim; but you also, Judah, set a harvest for yourself, when I shall turn back the captivity of my people. LXX: In the house of Israel I have seen horrible things, there the fornication of Ephraim; Israel and Judah have been defiled; begin your vintage when I shall turn back the captivity of my people. Of this crime and terrible horror Jeremiah too speaks: The heaven was astounded at this, and the earth shuddered exceedingly. For what is more horrible than that the ten tribes suddenly went over to the worship of idols? Hence it is said to their metropolis: Take away your calf, Samaria, in which Ephraim first played the harlot, that is, Jeroboam of the tribe of Ephraim; and while he played the harlot, Israel was defiled, namely the people of Samaria, which for the most part held the common name of Israel.

But in the house of the heretics we see a horrible thing daily, the teachers first playing the harlot, and the people who are led on by them being defiled. Judah too, that is, the Church, is commanded that it too should prepare for itself, because of its sins, a harvest, or a vintage, when the time of judgment comes. But it is pardoned, and the Lord promises it forgiveness, because whom he loves he rebukes, and he chastises every son whom he receives, so that, tested and purged, he may store him in his treasuries. Some refer what is said: Judah, begin your vintage, or, set a harvest for yourself, to the good sense, so that, Israel having been punished, this one receives the fruits of its works, according to what is written: Those who sow in tears will reap in joy. To us the former sense is more pleasing.

6:11.t: Hence the word is turned to Judah also: You too, Judah, set a harvest for yourself; and the sense is: Do not think yourself secure because Israel is led away captive; you too, prepare your crops to be reaped; for not much later you will be led captive to Babylon, and the time of your reaping will come. And when the Chaldeans have reaped you, I will turn back again the captivity of my people, and under Cyrus king of the Persians and Artaxerxes I will bring my people back. And note how pointedly the captivity of Judah and its return are prophesied together; but of Israel, that is, of the ten tribes, there is silence even now, and if ever something favorable is said, it is put off to the coming of Christ.

7:1.t: When I wished to heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim was uncovered, and the malice of Samaria, because they have wrought a lie; and the thief has entered, the robber plundering outside. LXX: likewise. Israel often received many wounds of idolatry, and above all that one when in the desert they cast the head of a calf and said: These are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. Hence I, who prefer the repentance of the sinner to his death, and who afterwards say in the Gospel: The healthy have no need of a physician, but those who are sick, have tried to heal the wounds of my people. And while I was treating these with every art, so that the wretched people might be cured, suddenly Jeroboam of the tribe of Ephraim arose, to make the golden calves, and the malice of Samaria, which followed the impious king, was uncovered; for both king and people wrought a lie, that is, an idol. For just as an image is contrary to God, so a lie is contrary to the truth. […]

7:2.t: Therefore each one must keep his heart with all watchfulness, for when the Lord comes in the day of judgment, "He will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts," "all the thoughts of men meanwhile accusing or else excusing them," "when their own devices have beset them about." But of such a nature are the evil thoughts that sometimes they make worthy of censure even those things which seem good and which, so far as the popular judgment is concerned, are indeed worthy of praise.
7:2.s: COMMENTARY ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 11:15

7:2.t: And lest perhaps they say in their hearts that I have remembered all their wickedness, now their devices have surrounded them; they have been done before my face. LXX: That they may sing together as those who sing in their hearts: I have remembered all their wickednesses; now their thoughts have surrounded them, they have been done against my face. Lest perhaps, he says, they say in their hearts: God has brought old sins back upon us, and we are paying for the offenses of our fathers; they ate the sour grape, and our teeth were set on edge; for that reason I will recount in the following discourse what they have done now and at present, while I look on, and what they do daily; and I will show them their devices, or the thoughts with which they have most zealously pursued evil, and the things they have done in my presence, not fearing my face. […]

7:3.t: In their wickedness they made the king glad, and in their lies the princes. LXX: In their wickednesses they made the kings glad, and in their lies the princes. He sets out what they did before his face: In their wickednesses they made King Jeroboam glad, and in their lies the princes who had been set over the people under Jeroboam. The heretics too, in the wickedness of their works, have made the king, the devil, glad, and in the lies of their perverse dogmas, the princes, no doubt those of this world, whose false wisdom God destroys. Among the heretics we can call king the one who first invented the heresy, and princes those who, set over the peoples of the heretics, claim for themselves a false priesthood. And at the same time it must be noted that the opposing powers and the rulers and princes of this darkness rejoice in our sins.

7:4.t: But where shall I find on a sudden the divine Scripture which may teach me what the "oven" is? I must call upon my Lord Jesus, that he may make me who seek to find, and open to me who knock, so that I may find in the Scriptures the "oven" where I may cook my sacrifice, so that God may receive it. And indeed I think I have found it in the prophet Hosea, where he says: "all committing adultery, like an oven heated for burning", and again: "their hearts," he says, "grew hot like an oven". The heart of man, then, is the "oven". But this heart, if vices set it ablaze or the devil inflames it, will not cook, but will burn up. But if he set it ablaze who said: "I came to cast fire upon the earth", then the loaves of the divine Scriptures and of the words of God, which I receive in my heart, I do not burn up to destruction, but cook for a sacrifice.

All are adulterers, like an oven heated by the baker; the city rested a little from the mixing of the leaven, until the whole was leavened. LXX: All are adulterers, like an oven burning for baking, to the scorching of the flame, from the mixing of the leaven, until the whole was leavened. Those who in their wickedness made the king glad, and in their lies the princes, are all adulterers; and like an oven they were heated by Jeroboam with the fire of idolatry, so as to bake the bread of impiety; and he, when he had sent the burning of error into their souls, like a furnace and an oven first heated with fire, rested a little, so as not to force the people but to leave them to their own will, until the whole lie was leavened; for whatever is done by compulsion is quickly undone, but what we seize upon by our will endures. […]

Those who bent their knee to drink are those who inclined themselves totally to philosophy: and the same are inclined to an infinite number of errors, and that is how the leaven of error is warmed. As Osee writes, "the city rested a little from the mingling of the leaven, till the whole was leavened." They warm the eggs of asps, so that what has been warmed breaks out into a serpent.

7:5.t: The day of our king: the princes began to rage from wine; he stretched out his hand with the mockers, because they applied their heart like an oven when he lay in wait for them. All night he slept baking them; in the morning he himself was kindled like a fire of flame; all were heated like an oven and devoured their judges; all their kings have fallen; there is none among them who cries to me. LXX: The day of your kings. The princes began to rage from wine; he stretched out his hand with the pestilent, because their hearts were kindled like an oven, while they were cast down headlong all night. Ephraim was filled with sleep; morning came; he was set on fire like a flame of fire. All were heated like an oven, a burning fire, and they ate up their judges. All their kings have fallen; there is not among them one who calls on me. An obscure passage, and one needing the close attention of the reader, so that we may first learn the history. […]

Now let us pass to the spiritual understanding: Unhappy peoples who are led astray by the king, the devil, and by his princes; or who have taken up other solemn feasts from the prince of a heresy and from his leaders, leaving the Church and trampling on the truth of the faith, are accustomed to shout and say: This is the day of our king; for example, of Valentinus, of Marcion, of Arius and of Eunomius. Those set over them, hearing this, are not made drunk with wine, lest the sin be thought a light one, but they rave from the wine of which Moses writes in the song of Deuteronomy: Their wine is the fury of dragons, and the incurable fury of asps; for these eat the food of impiety and are made drunk with the wine of iniquity. Of this the Apostle also says: Do not be drunk with wine, in which is debauchery. And in Proverbs we read: Let princes not drink wine, lest they forget wisdom and be unable to judge rightly. […]

7:6.t: These mockers, when their king lay in wait for them and was leading them away from their God, offered him their heart like an oven, for him to kindle them and make them burn with the flames of idolatry. For he assented to the people for this reason: because he understood that they had turned to error with their whole mind. And what follows: All night he slept baking them; in the morning he himself was kindled like a fire of flame, signifies this: after he sent fire into the oven of their heart, and saw them raging, and that there was no one to resist his will, he slept all night, that is, he was secure; he kept himself in darkness while they were being baked and were making the bread of impiety. Hence afterwards he rose in the morning, and showed the flame of his crimes in open madness, so that they passed over, no longer by stealth but shamelessly, from the worship of God to the ceremonies of idols.

7:7.t: What more? All, like an oven, were heated with the fire of idolatry, and devoured their judges, so that even one who could have been good by nature and could have remembered the religion of the Lord, seeing both princes and people subject to the calves and thinking them gods, is himself also devoured by the crime. Finally, all the kings of Israel fell, and walked in the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin, and none was found who abandoned the idols and returned to God. These things we have spoken according to the tradition of the Hebrews, more boldly than knowingly, leaving the credit for what is said to its authors.

Their hearts are heated by various passions: anger, love, avarice; and they devour their judges, either whatever virtues they may be able to have in their mind, or the senses by which they distinguish evil from good. Or else it must be said that the leaders of the heretics are devoured by their own peoples, so that they themselves are devoured by the assent of those whose houses they devour for the sake of base gain. All the princes of the heretics have fallen; although they cry to the Lord, there is none who calls on his name. For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among those who call on his name; they called on the Lord, and he heard them, he who does not hear the kings and princes of the heretics, because there is none among them who cries to the Lord.

7:8.t: But, to pass to another sense: though Ephraim ought to teach the peoples and draw them to his own likeness, he himself is mingled with the peoples and becomes like them; according to what was said above: As the people is, so will the priest be. Or Ephraim is mingled with the peoples and the nations, so that all heretics differ in nothing from the error of the Gentiles. And he who was once a leader in the Church has become a loaf baked under the ashes, surrounded on every side by unclean ash and the heat of the fires, so that he did not return to the Lord but persisted in the error he had begun.

Ephraim himself was mingled among the peoples; Ephraim has become a loaf baked under the ashes, which is not turned over; strangers devoured his strength, and he did not know it. Yes, and grey hairs were spread over him, and he was unaware of it; and the pride of Israel will be humbled before his face, and they have not returned to the Lord their God, and they have not sought him in all these things. LXX: Ephraim was mingled with his peoples; Ephraim has become a loaf baked under the ashes, which is not turned over. Strangers devoured his strength, but he did not know it; and grey hairs blossomed on him, and he was unaware of it; and the insolence of Israel will be humbled before his face, and they have not returned to the Lord their God; and they have not sought him in all these things. The kingdom of the ten tribes became like all the nations, because they withdrew from the Lord; […]

Ephraim is a cake under the ashes not turned. For a cake under the ashes, that hath ashes upon it, lays the cleaner side flat to the ground, and has the upper side the fouler, in proportion as it carries the ashes upon it. And so with the mind that harbours earthly thoughts, what else does it carry upon itself but a load of ashes? But if it will be 'turned,' the clean surface, which it had kept downwards, it brings back to the top, when it has shaken off the ashes that it had upon it. If therefore we shake off from the mind the ashes of earthly thoughts, as it were we 'turn the cake under the ashes,' that that bent of our mind may henceforth go to the rear, which the ashes of grovelling thought before overlaid, and the clean face come to the top, that our right bent of mind may not henceforth be surcharged with the weight of earthly desire. Which we can never do, except we be bedewed with the grace of the Holy Spirit, in that when Almighty God 'sendeth out the waters, they will overturn the earth.'
7:8.s: Morals on the Book of Job, Book XI, Section 10

7:9.t: Demons devoured his strength, for these are the strangers and the enemies of all Christians, and he did not know it, thinking his adversaries friends, and judging those who devoured him to be his table-companions; yes, and grey hairs were spread over him, or rather they blossomed, that is, he went astray for a long time; and nonetheless he was unaware of his old age and his decrepitude, of which it is written: What grows old and ages is near to destruction. And if it is said of a just man and a churchman: A man's grey hairs are his wisdom, why should it not be said of an unjust man and a heretic: A man's grey hairs are his folly? Of this old age Daniel spoke to the elder: You who have grown old in evil days. Hence also in the book of the Shepherd — if, however, anyone cares to accept the reading of it — the Church appears to Hermas first with a grey head, then as a young girl and a bride adorned with her tresses.

Moses: Just as all young men are not alike in fervour of spirit nor equally instructed in learning and good morals, so too we cannot find that all old men are equally perfect and excellent. For the true riches of old men are not to be measured by grey hairs but by their diligence in youth and the rewards of their past labours. "For," says one, "the things that thou hast not gathered in thy youth, how shall thou find them in thy old age?" "For venerable old age is not that of long time, nor counted by the number of years: but the understanding of a man is grey hairs, and a spotless life is old age." And therefore we are not to follow in the steps or embrace the traditions and advice of every old man whose head is covered with grey hairs, and whose age is his sole claim to respect, but only of those whom we find to have distinguished themselves in youth in an approved and praiseworthy manner, and to have been trained up not on self-assurance but on the traditions of the Elders. […]
7:9.s: Second Conference of Abbot Moses, Chapter 13

7:9.t: Abraham: I will not give you my own opinion against this, but that of the blessed Antony, whereby he confounded the laziness of a certain brother (overcome by this luke-warmness which you describe) in such a way as also to cut the knot of your subject. For when one came as I said to the aforesaid old man, and said that the Anchorite system was not at all to be admired, declaring that it required greater virtue for a man to practise what belongs to perfection living among men rather than in the desert, the blessed Antony asked Where he lived himself, and when he said that he lived close to his relations, and boasted that by their provision he was set free from all care and anxiety of daily work, and gave himself up ceaselessly and solely to reading and prayer without any distraction of spirit, once more the blessed Antony said: "Tell me, my good friend, whether you grieve with their griefs and misfortunes, and in the same way rejoice in their good fortune?" He confessed that he shared in them both. […]

Strangers have devoured his strength, and he hath known it not. For by 'strangers' are usually understood apostate angels, who devour our strength, when they consume the virtue of the mind by perverting it. Which Ephraim both endured, and knew it not, because through the temptation of malignant spirits he both lost the strength of his mind, and understood not that he had lost it. Want therefore goes before the face of Leviathan, because he spoils by his temptation the minds of the careless, before he who is tempted knows his snares.
7:9.s: Morals on the Book of Job, Book XXXIV, Section 6

7:10.t: Hence the pride of Israel will be humbled, not after a long time, but now and in the present; for this is what he means by before his face; and it was being humbled because it had lifted itself up and trusted not in God but in the size of its army, and because God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble; for pride, that is, gaon, the Seventy, after their custom, translated ὕβριν, that is, outrage. And because he had said above: Ephraim has become a loaf baked under the ashes which is not turned over, and this seemed ambiguous and did not make clear enough what he meant, he now puts it more plainly: They have not returned to the Lord their God; and they have not sought him in all these things. For if they had returned to the Lord their God, they would surely have heard God speaking through Jeremiah: Return to me, and I will return to you. And though they had done so much, they did not seek him whom they had lost through their own fault.

And though the pride of the heretics is humbled, or the insolence which they daily offer to churchmen, they do not return to the Lord; but in all these things they by no means seek him, because they have been heated like an oven, and they have not sought him; they have devoured their judges, and the kings fell together; nor is there anyone who cries to the Lord. All these things they suffered so that they might seek the Lord, whom they refused to seek.

7:11.t: And Ephraim has become like a dove led astray, without heart. They called upon Egypt, they went off to the Assyrians; and when they have set out, I will spread my net over them, I will bring them down like a bird of the sky, I will strike them according to the report of their assembly. LXX: And Ephraim was like a foolish dove without heart. He called upon Egypt, and they went off into the Assyrians as they will go. I will cast my net over them, I will bring them down like the birds of the sky; I will correct them in the hearing of their tribulation. The Lord commands in the Gospel that we be simple as doves and shrewd as serpents, so that, imitating the simplicity of doves and the shrewdness of the serpent, we may neither be able to harm others nor suffer snares from others; but by simplicity and prudence may show ourselves balanced men, because prudence without goodness is malice, and simplicity without reason is called folly. Ephraim therefore has become like a dove led astray, in Hebrew photha; […]

The question is asked why Ephraim is compared not to other birds but to the dove. The other birds hasten to protect their young even at the peril of their own life; and when they see a hawk, a snake, a raven or a crow approaching their nest, they fly about hither and thither, and hurl themselves at the attacker with their bites, and tear it with their claws, and testify to a parent's grief with plaintive cries; the dove alone does not grieve for its young when they are taken away, and does not look for them; and to it Ephraim is rightly compared, because he does not perceive that his people is being laid waste piece by piece, but is careless of his own safety.

Let us read Hosea the prophet, and we find his whole prophecy against Ephraim; and it is said there: "Ephraim," it says, "has become like a foolish dove." See what he says: "a foolish dove." It has abandoned the temple, and dwells in the woods. For the dove always dwells in houses. But Ephraim, my dove, has abandoned the temple, has abandoned the house, and dwells in the woods, dwells in the deserts.

And what he says: I will strike them according to the report of their assembly, can also mean this: just as by a common counsel they all fashioned idols, so, when I am angered, they will all be laid waste together. The teachers of contrary dogmas, who have abandoned Christ, the Wisdom, and have gone out from the Church, we can rightly call a foolish and heartless dove, since, desiring earthly things, they have been handed over to the Assyrians. And when they have set out from the Church, the Lord spreads his net, woven from the testimonies of the Scriptures and the skilful discourse of wisdom, so as to bring down to low places those who lift themselves up against the knowledge of God and, like a bird, fly to the heights; and to correct them by threats and by the hearing of punishments, so that, corrected, they may not perish for ever.

And the prophet of God abuseth those who are foolish in respect of good things, and wise in respect of evil things. "Ephraim is like a silly dove, without understanding; he cometh to Egypt and he goeth to Assyria, and in the way of repentance towards Me he walketh not." Now the prophet maketh an accusation against such silliness, because it is not simplicity, but folly. And this also is the wickedness of those who are silly in respect of good things. Instead of one Redeemer, they have chosen unto themselves many helpers, and they have forsaken the path which leadeth to God, and have run after the Egyptians and Assyrians that they might come to their help. And although they have experienced many times that they were not able to redeem them from the evils in which they stood, they never became wise enough through the experience of facts to run to God's place of refuge. And the prophet likened them unto doves whose fruit others carried off, and the children of whose bowels were made servants unto others; […]
7:11.s: 13 Ascetic Discourses, Discourse 5 -- Second Discourse on Simplicity

7:12.t: And so that God might show that by changing places we cannot escape his eyes, and that we are always ruled by the power of God: When, he says, they have set out into the Assyrians, even there I will spread my net, and if they have been lifted up like birds, I will bring them down from there. But I will bring them down, not to destruction, but to strike them as sons; and I will strike them not with the greatness of punishments, but with fear, so that, hearing of the punishments of old, they may be corrected by terrors alone.

And the prophet seeing that all the remedies of this life will have been applied in vain for their healing, and already as it were despairing of their life, declares: "The bellows have failed in the fire, the founder hath melted in vain: for their wicked deeds are not consumed. Call them reprobate silver, for the Lord hath rejected them." And the Lord thus laments that to no purpose has He applied this salutary cleansing by fire to those who are hardened in their sins, in the person of Jerusalem crusted all over with the rust of her sins, when He says: "set it empty upon burning coals, that it may be hot, and the brass thereof may be melted; and let the filth of it be melted in the midst thereof. Great pains have been taken, and the great rust thereof is not gone out, no not even by fire. Thy uncleanness is execrable: because I desired to cleanse thee, and thou art not cleansed from thy filthiness." […]

7:13.t: Woe to them, because they have withdrawn from me; they will be laid waste, because they have transgressed against me. I redeemed them, and they have spoken lies against me, and they have not cried to me in their heart, but they howled on their beds. LXX: Woe to them, because they have withdrawn from me; they are manifest, because they have acted impiously against me; but I redeemed them; yet they have spoken a lie against me, and their hearts have not cried to me, but they howled on their beds. While I was spreading my net to catch them, and to bring them down from their pride like a bird of the sky, and to strike them in the hearing of their distress, they withdrew and leapt away from me; for this is what ἀπεπήδησαν means, which the Seventy used in their translation. And therefore they will be laid waste, because they have transgressed against me. Where we said: they will be laid waste, in the Hebrew is written sod laem, that is, devastation to them. Symmachus translated it destruction; Theodotion, misery. […]

7:14.t:
They ruminated on wheat and wine, they withdrew from me.

And I taught them and strengthened their arms; and they devised malice against me; they returned so as to be without a yoke; they have become like a deceitful bow; their princes will fall by the sword, from the fury of their tongue; this is their derision in the land of Egypt. LXX: On wheat and wine they were cutting themselves; they were taught in me, and I strengthened their arms, and they devised evils against me; they turned to nothing, they became like a bent bow; their princes will fall by the sword because of the unskilfulness of their tongue; such is their derision in the land of Egypt. Because of the abundance of all things, he says, they fell. Ezekiel too records that this happened in Sodom and Gomorrah, so that they ruminated on nothing but food and luxury; […]

On wheat and wine, and the false mysteries of the body and blood of Christ, who says in the Gospel: Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone. And in another place: I am the true vine. And: Unless you drink my blood. Over this wheat and wine, then, the heretics are cut asunder, and build diverse tabernacles for themselves; or they are cut off from the body of the Church, and pretend to meditate on the law of God and to ruminate on it. But in doing this they withdraw from the Lord, who taught them in the Church and gave them strength with which to fight against the adversaries.

7:15.t: But they devised malice against the Lord, building up most impious heresies, and returned to the state of the Gentiles, so as to be without the knowledge and the yoke of God; or they returned to nothing, not that they ceased to be, but because, in comparison with him who speaks to Moses: Go, say to the people of Israel: He who is has sent me, all who think against the Lord are said not to be. According to what we read in Esther, in the Seventy only. Do not hand over your scepter to those who are not: there is no doubt that it means idols. For if God is truth, whatever is contrary to truth is a lie, and is called nothing. This fits the heretics, who, instructed from the holy Scriptures, turn the words of the law and the prophets and the Gospel against the Lord; and they are like a deceitful or perverse bow. A deceitful and perverse bow is one that strikes the one who aims it, and wounds its own master. Or they have become like a bent bow, always ready for battle and contentions, to the subversion of their hearers. […]

7:16.t: And as they were from the beginning, before I called them through Abraham and afterwards through Moses and Aaron, when they were without the yoke and the knowledge of the law and were mingled with all the nations, so even now they have returned to their former state, so as to be carried without yoke and bridle over precipices, and to be changed into a deceitful bow; so that the bow which God had bent against the adversaries they themselves turned against their own Lord, and shot against him the arrows of blasphemies. Hence their princes, who deceived the unhappy people, will fall by the sword because of the fury of their tongue, with which they dared to call the golden calves gods, so that they did in the land of promise what they had learned in Egypt, worshiping the Egyptian Apis and venerating all their monstrosities. For so also in the wilderness, when they had come out of Egypt, they derided the Lord, saying: These are your gods, Israel. […]

8:1.t: Let there be a trumpet in your throat, like an eagle over the house of the Lord; because they have transgressed my covenant and violated my law. They called upon me: My God, we know you, Israel. Israel has cast away the good; the enemy will pursue him. They have reigned, and not from me: they have been princes, and I did not know it. Of their silver and gold they have made idols for themselves, that they might perish. LXX: In their bosom like earth, like an eagle over the house of the Lord, because they have transgressed my testament and acted impiously against my law. They called upon me: God, we know you; because Israel has turned away from good things. They pursued the enemy, they reigned for themselves and not through me; they have been princes, and they did not make it known to me; of their silver and their gold they have made idols for themselves, that they might utterly perish. […]

The devil, who longs to set his nest above the stars of heaven, we very often read called an eagle: If you are exalted like an eagle, from there I will bring you down, says the Lord. The eye too that mocks its father and despises the old age of its mother will be dug out by ravens, and the young of eagles will devour it; losing the clear light of its vision through the devil and the demons. Hence it is commanded in the law that we should not eat the eagle. This eagle, then, comes upon the conventicles of the heretics, which were once the house of the Lord; and it comes because they have transgressed his covenant and abandoned the law of God; and in vain they call upon him and say: You are my God, and we know you, we who are called Israel, seeing God, and are called by the Christian name. In vain, he says, they do these things, since they have set up kings for themselves, and acted against my will, and have as princes my adversaries, whom I do not know, because they do not deserve knowledge of me. […]

8:2.t: Hence in the time of necessity and distress, when the captivity comes, they will call upon me and say: My God, we know you, Israel; we who are called Israel know you and acknowledge you, and we keep the ancient name of Jacob, who pleased you, so that we are called Israel.

8:3.t: To them the Lord replied: How are you called Israel, when Israel has cast away the good, that is, his Lord, from whom he was called Israel? Therefore, because Israel cast away the good, the enemy, that is, the Assyrian, will pursue him and seize him, who, having abandoned me as king, asked for a king for themselves, as the other nations also had, and acted against my will. Finally, Samuel for this reason sets before them the harsh commands of a king, and says that their sons and daughters will serve kings, so that they might return to the Lord, the most merciful king; but they became princes without the will of God. And this crime was not enough for them, unless they doubled the outrage with a greater impiety, turning into idols the silver and gold which they had received for riches and adornment. Therefore Saul became king not by the will of God, but by the error of the people. And because he did not have the root of piety, as soon as he began to reign he was inflamed with impiety. […]

8:4.t: Not always is the prince of the people and judge of the Church given by the judgment of God, but according as our merits demand. If our deeds are evil and we "work evil in the sight of God", princes are given to us according to our heart; and this I will prove to you from the Scriptures. For hear what the Lord says: "They made themselves a king and not by me, and a prince and not by my counsel". And this seems to be said of that Saul, whom indeed the Lord himself had chosen and had commanded to be made king; but because he had been chosen not according to the will of God, but according to the merit of a sinful people, he denies that he was appointed with his will or counsel.

When Peter is speaking to the people concerning the bishop to be ordained in the place of Judas, it says, "Peter stood up in the midst of the disciples, for the multitude was together." But we notice that the apostles observed this, not only in the ordination of bishops and of priests but also in the ordinations of deacons. Concerning this very thing, in their Acts, it is also written, "The Twelve called together the multitude of the disciples," it says, "and spoke to them."6This matter was carried on diligently and cautiously, with the whole people assembled so that no unworthy man should attain to the ministry of the altar or to the priestly rank. For the fact is that sometimes unworthy men are ordained, not according to the will of God but according to human presumption. These things that do not come from a legitimate and just ordination are displeasing to God. God himself makes this known through the prophet Hosea, saying, "They made themselves a king, but not by me."

Because He is exceedingly desirous, that we should always take refuge in Him, and in everything make our requests unto Him; and do nothing and speak nothing without Him. For men, when we trouble them repeatedly concerning our affairs, become slothful and evasive, and conduct themselves unpleasantly towards us; but with God it is quite the reverse. Not when we apply to him continually respecting our affairs, but when we fail to do so, then is he especially displeased. Hear at least what He reproves the Jews for, when He says, "Ye have taken counsel, but not of Me, and made treaties, but not by My Spirit." For this is the custom of those who love; they desire that all the concerns of their beloved should be accomplished by means of themselves; and that they should neither do anything, nor say anything, without them. On this account did God not only on that occasion, but again elsewhere, uttering a reproof, speak the same language. "They have reigned, but not by Me; they have ruled, and they made it not known to Me."

But it can be reasonably asked, How it is said in this place that the Lord makes the hypocrite to reign, when by the Prophet He complains especially of this thing, saying, They have reigned, but not of Me: they have become princes, and I know them not? For, who that thinks rightly, can say that the Lord does that of which He knows nothing? But, because God's knowledge is approval, His ignorance is disapproval. Whence He says to some whom He rejects, I know you not whence ye are; depart from Me, all ye workers of iniquity. And sometimes God's doing a thing, is His allowing in His anger that which He forbids to be done. Hence He asserted that He hardened the heart of the king of Egypt, because He, in truth, allowed it to be hardened. In a marvellous manner then does God make hypocrites to reign, and knows them not. He makes them, by suffering; He knows them not, by rejecting them. Whence it is necessary, with reference to every thing, which is desired in this life, that the Inner Will should be first enquired into. […]
8:4.s: Morals on the Book of Job, Book XXV, Section 41

8:5.t: What he had said above: Of their silver and their gold they have made idols for themselves, that they might perish, he now explains more plainly: Your calf is cast off, Samaria, my fury is kindled against them; either against the calves, because they had made two; or against the inhabitants of Samaria, who worshiped them. Moreover, as for what we read in the Seventy: Cast off your calf, Samaria, he exhorts its inhabitants, not of one city but of all the ten tribes, which are called Samaria — for otherwise there were no calves in the city of Samaria, but in Dan and in Bethel — to cast off the calves against which God is angry; or ἀποτρίψεται, that is, let it rub them away; so that it may little by little rub away and cleanse those which it had worshiped for a long time. And when they do not listen, he turns to others, and speaks as though to a third person: how long will they be unable to be cleansed? What madness is this, he says, that, while I give room for repentance, they refuse to turn to health?

God casts off the calves of the heretics and of Samaria, who say that they keep the precepts of the law; which calves cling to the ground and work in the earth, not in the spirit, nor lift their eyes to heaven; and therefore the fury of the Lord is kindled against them, and he wonders what this great perversity is, that they will not abandon the idols which they have fashioned for themselves, and love heretical filth instead of the cleanness of the Church. These calves Israel, who pretends that he sees God, did not receive from the other nations; but he himself forged for himself out of the holy Scriptures the depravity of his understanding, and he is the craftsman of his own god, which will quickly perish and will imitate spiders' webs, which are broken at a light touch.

8:6.t: Your calf is cast off, Samaria. My fury is kindled against them. How long will they be unable to be cleansed? For it too is from Israel; a craftsman made it, and it is not God, for the calf of Samaria will become spiders' webs. LXX: Cast off your calf, Samaria; my fury is roused against them. How long will they be unable to be cleansed in Israel? And this a craftsman made, and it is not God, because your calf, Samaria, was leading astray. In the place where we have put spiders' webs, in the Hebrew is written sababim, with the letter iod as the penultimate; not, as some falsely think, sababum, that is, with uau, which the Seventy and Theodotion translated πλανῶν, that is, leading astray and deceiving; Aquila, wandering or turned about; Symmachus, inconstant or unstable, that is, ἀκαταστατῶν; the Fifth edition, ῥεμβεύων, roving and fluctuating. […]

And because he had said: Cast off your calf, Samaria, he explains who this calf is: for it too is from Israel; not from others, he says, from the nations, have you received the calf, as Baal and Ashtaroth from the Sidonians, as Chemosh from the Moabites and Moloch from the Ammonites; but you yourselves, and your king Jeroboam, made in Israel what you had learned in Egypt. Or what sort of god is that which is formed by the hand of a craftsman? Finally, as the threads of spiders dissolve into the wind, so the calf of Samaria will be reduced to nothing.

8:7.t: For they will sow the wind and reap the whirlwind; there is no standing stalk in it, the shoot will make no flour, and if it should make any, strangers will eat it. LXX: For they have sown things corrupted by the wind, and their overthrow will receive them; a sheaf without the strength to make flour, and if it should make any, strangers will eat it. He compares the calf of Samaria to spiders' webs; therefore he keeps the metaphor in what follows, so that what he had called spiders' webs he compares to wind and whirlwind, and to stalks that do not stand; and if they do stand, they have no flour; and if, he says, they should make flour, it will be devoured by others. And since the sense is common both to the heretics and to those in Samaria who fashioned idols, it must be discussed in common. These men sow the wind, or seeds corrupted by the wind, which have no pith, which the Greeks call ἐντεριώνην, and therefore, sowing empty things, they receive what is void and empty; […]

For it is infinite folly to labour painfully, and pant after the breath of applause, to apply one's self to the heavenly precepts with hard toil, but to aim at the reward of an earthly kind of recompense. For that I may so express myself, he that in return for the good that he practises looks for the applause of his fellowcreatures, is carrying an article of great worth to be sold at a mean price. From that whereby he might have earned the kingdom of heaven, he seeks the coin of passing talk. His practice goes for little, in that he spends a great deal, and gets back but very little. Whereunto then are hypocrites like but to luxuriant and untended vines, which put forth fruit from their fertility, but are never lifted from the earth by tending? […]
8:7.s: Morals on the Book of Job, Book VIII, Sections 70-71

8:8.t: Israel has been devoured; now he has become among the nations like an unclean vessel. The Seventy translated "useless" for "unclean"; the rest likewise. The unclean, or useless, vessel the Hebrews call a chamber pot, which we are accustomed to use for receiving and throwing away excrement. To this uncleanness he compares the idolaters and the heretics, who are mingled with the Gentiles while they do not keep the truth of God, and, having been made a vessel unto honor, have been turned into a vessel of dishonor. For what is more unclean than a demonic spirit and the dogmas of the heretics, which have mingled them with the pagans? Such was Jeconiah, enslaved to idols, of whom God speaks through Jeremiah: Jeconiah is dishonored, like a vessel of which there is no use. On the contrary Paul, who could say: Or do you seek a proof of Christ who speaks in me? is called a chosen vessel, of gold and of silver, because he had wisdom and eloquence, with which he preached the Gospel of Christ. […]

8:9.t: For they themselves have gone up to Assyria, a wild ass alone by himself. Ephraim have given gifts to lovers; moreover they have hired the nations for pay; now I will gather them, and they will rest a little while from the burden of the king and of the princes. LXX: For they themselves have gone up to the Assyrians; Ephraim has sprouted within himself, they have loved gifts; therefore they will be handed over among the Gentiles; now I will receive them, and they will rest a little, that they may anoint kings and princes. Israel, he says, has been devoured, and has become like a useless, or unclean, vessel, of which no potsherd remains in which water could be drawn, or some small bit of fire. And because he has become an unclean vessel, therefore they have gone up to the Assyrians, imitating the solitary wild ass; not at all as sheep fed by the Lord, but wickedly abusing their freedom, and led away into captivity; […]

As for the heretics, we do not doubt that, going to the Assyrians according to the error of their mind, they think that they are ascending, not descending. Hence it is said to them through Isaiah: What has happened to you now, that you have all gone up onto empty roofs? The prince of these Assyrians is the great mind. Hence Ephraim has sprouted within himself, judging in his presumption that he has grown. Or he has become a solitary wild ass, so as to enter not the planted fields of the Church but the deserts of the devil. He has loved gifts in return for his error, promising himself rewards, or doing everything for the sake of shameful gain. Or at least he has given gifts and payments to his lovers, the demons, and when he has done this, he will be handed over to the Gentiles. For just as the nations worship bodily images, so these men think to be gods the idols which they have fashioned out of their own heart, and therefore they will be reckoned among the number of the nations.

8:10.t: And when they have given presents to the Gentiles, and have hired the nations for pay to help them, they will be gathered for battle, and, bound, will be led away together. And because they love to offer gifts to their adversaries, therefore for a little while they will obtain the favor of not paying tribute to the king and the princes, until they come to the Assyrians, where they will by no means pay taxes and tribute as free men, but will be reduced to the utmost slavery.

But if, he says, now and in the present age they repent, and I receive them, they will cease to set up over themselves the little king and his princes; so that we may understand the little king to be the devil, in distinction from the great king, who can have no fellowship with Belial, but, as soon as he has been received, drives the little king and his princes out of the heart of believers. According to the Hebrew, however, those who had before been scattered, and had hired the nations for pay, will be gathered into the Church of God, and will rest from the burden of the king, about whom the Apostle rebukes those cut off from the Church, saying: Without us you reign; and would that you did reign, and from the princes whom they have, set up in the synagogues of the devil.

8:11.t: For Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning; altars have become for him an offense. I will write for him my manifold laws, which have been reckoned as foreign; bring victims, bring; they will sacrifice flesh and eat it, and the Lord will not accept them. LXX: For Ephraim has multiplied altars, for sin, altars are beloved to him. I will write for them a multitude; his ordinances have been reckoned as foreign, beloved altars; for if they have sacrificed victims and eaten flesh, the Lord will not accept them.
