Led, he says, into captivity, they will rest for a little while from the burden of the king and the prince. And they will suffer this because Ephraim, their prince, has multiplied altars, not on which to sacrifice to the Lord, but on which to join sins to sins; and these altars, that is, places of sacrifice, will be turned for him into an offense, so that the more of them there are, the more his crimes are multiplied.

Now the Apostle teaches that there is one altar in the Church, and one faith, and one baptism; deserting this, the heretics have fashioned for themselves many altars, not for appeasing God, but for a multitude of offenses. Therefore they do not deserve to receive the law of God, since they had earlier despised those laws which they had received. And if they have said anything from the Scriptures, it is to be compared not with the divine words, but with the thoughts of the pagans. These men sacrifice many victims and eat their flesh, deserting the one victim of Christ; nor do they eat the flesh of him whose flesh is the food of believers. Whatever they do, feigning the order and rite of sacrifices, whether they give alms, or promise chastity, or feign humility and deceive all the simple with pretended blandishments, the Lord will accept nothing of sacrifices of this kind.

8:12.t: Then, as he had said above: What shall I do to you, Ephraim? What shall I do to you, Judah? as though hesitating and seeking with what remedy he might heal the sick man, and by what counsels he might draw the sinner back to salvation. I will write for them again, he says, the laws which I had given before through Moses. But what profit is there in writing still others, when he has despised those which he received before? Is it not contempt of God when, though I commanded that there should be one altar in Jerusalem, they fashioned idols on all the mountains and hills with which to provoke the Lord?

8:13.t: They also made altars for this reason, not to please me, but so that, when many victims had been sacrificed, they might eat their flesh, according to what the Lord says in the Gospel: Amen, amen, I say to you, you seek me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled. For they put all their zeal for victims into devouring the sacrifices, not into pleasing God through them; nor will the Lord accept those which they sacrificed not to him, but to their own belly and gullet.

Now he will remember their iniquity and will visit their sins; they will be turned back into Egypt.

And Israel has forgotten his Maker and has built shrines, and Judah has multiplied fortified cities; and I will send fire upon his cities, and it will devour his dwellings. LXX: Now he will remember their iniquities, and will avenge their injustices; they have turned back into Egypt, and Israel has forgotten him who made him, and they have built shrines, and Judah has multiplied walled cities; and I will send forth fire upon his cities, and it will devour his foundations. Between ἀνομίαν, that is, iniquity, and sin there is this difference, that iniquities are before the law, sin is after the law; and for those who persist in their offenses, the Lord will remember their iniquity, which they had committed before the law; but their sins he will not remember, but will take vengeance on them. […]

But according to anagogy, those are called iniquities, that is, both ἀνομίαι and ἀδικίαι (injustices), which we committed before baptism and which have been forgiven us in baptism; but sins are those which we have done after baptism, of which it is also written in the psalm: Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. All of these will be imputed to the heretics, so that both the old iniquities and the new sins are brought back upon them. For those who had gone out of Egypt through the confession of Christ have gone back into Egypt through faithlessness.

What we read according to the LXX translators, ÷ and in Assyria they ate unclean things :, is not found in the Hebrew, and therefore it must be marked beforehand with an obelus. We can, however, say that the Israelites, longing for Egypt, were taken captive by the Assyrians and there ate unclean things, according to Ezekiel, who describes them as having eaten food offered to idols in Chaldea, food so polluted with the filth of idols that it is compared to human dung. The heretics too, whose princes are the Assyrians — of whom we have often spoken — eat unclean things among them, while they are defiled by their filth.

8:14.t: For Israel has forgotten his Maker and has built shrines on the high places, consecrating whole hills and mountains, and shady trees, to Baal and Ashtaroth and other idols. Judah too, understanding that Israel had departed from the love of God and that their sins had been visited, was not converted to the Lord, but trusted in the fortification of his cities, which the Lord says he will destroy, devouring them down to his foundations. His: there is no doubt that it signifies Judah; although some read their foundations, that is, of the cities, in place of his.

Israel has forgotten his Maker, and, having despised the Creator, has fashioned another god for himself. Judah too, that is, the churchman, in evil works, or in a perverse interpretation of the holy Scriptures, has built himself fortified cities, not with the help of God, but with skillful falsehood; and the Lord says that he will set them on fire with the fire of his spirit, and will devour his βάρεις, that is, great houses built in the manner of towers, and will overturn the foundations badly laid, so that they may not be able to set up sacrilegious shrines against God. Some take the cities fortified by Judah in a good sense, and they try to temper what seemed contrary to this sense, I will send fire upon his cities, and it will devour his dwellings, in such a way that, after what is perfect has come, what is in part is destroyed.

9:1.t: Do not rejoice, Israel, do not exult like the peoples, for you have played the harlot away from your God; you have loved a payment upon all the threshing floors of wheat. The threshing floor and the winepress will not feed them, and the wine will deceive them. LXX: Do not be glad, Israel, and do not rejoice like the peoples, for you have played the harlot away from your God; you have loved gifts upon every threshing floor of wheat. The threshing floor and the winepress did not know them, and the wine has deceived them. Those who have departed from God, when they have come into the depth of sins and have despaired of their salvation, will despise everything. Finally Israel too, departing from the law of God and worshiping idols, says that he is one nation out of many nations, rejoicing and congratulating himself that he has departed from the knowledge of God and is a nation mingled with the rest; […]

It is said also to the heretics, that they should not exult and rejoice and think themselves like the other nations. For those did not believe in God; but these, under the name of God, worship idols and play the harlot away from their God; and they multiply for themselves many threshing floors and countless winepresses, and they eat the wheat from which the bread of mourning is made, and drink the wine of Sodom, which is trodden out with the gall of asps. And because they prepare for themselves many winepresses and many threshing floors, therefore they will not eat from the true and only threshing floor, nor drink from the winepress which the Lord Jesus trod; but whatever they think they have will be corrupted by falsehood.

9:2.t: You have reckoned many threshing floors and winepresses as the payment for your fornication, so that you might enjoy an abundance of all things; therefore the threshing floor and the winepress will not produce wheat and wine, and the winepress will deceive them, or will deny its wine, with which they thought they would be made drunk. We read that under Ahab king of Israel, and Elijah the prophet, there was a most severe famine in Samaria, so that mothers fed on the corpses of their own sons. At that time, according to the letter, the threshing floor and the winepress did not feed them, and the wine deceived them, and they wasted away in want.

9:3.t: They will not dwell in the land of the Lord; Ephraim has returned into Egypt, and among the Assyrians he has eaten what is polluted. They will not pour out wine to the Lord, and their sacrifices will not please him; like the bread of mourners, all who eat it will be defiled, because their bread, their own soul, will not enter into the house of the Lord. LXX: They did not dwell in the land of the Lord; Ephraim dwelt in Egypt, and among the Assyrians he ate what is unclean; they did not pour out wine to the Lord, nor did their sacrifices please him, because it is to them the bread of mourning; all who eat them will be defiled; because the loaves of their souls will not enter into the house of the Lord. Not only did the threshing floor and the winepress fail to feed them, and the wine lie in the land of Israel, when for three years and six months everything perished, but the inhabitants themselves also will depart from the land of the Lord; […]

They will not dwell in the land of the Lord who have departed from the Church, and have returned in mind into Egypt, and eat the sacrifices of the Assyrians, that is, of demons; nor do they pour out to the Lord the wine with which they have been made drunk unto luxury, and neither the things they offer nor they themselves who offer please him. The sacrifices of the heretics are the bread of mourning and of tears; for all that they do will be turned into weeping. Nor will they be able to hear: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted; but on the contrary they will hear: Woe to those who laugh, for they shall mourn. Whatever they offer, they offer not to God but to the dead, namely to those who have contrived wicked heresies; and whoever eats of their victims will be defiled. The blind will be led into the pit by the blind. Whatever they do, they do for the sake of delights, to deceive the people, to devour the houses of widows. […]

9:4.t: Let not the people flatter themselves as if they could be safe from contagion of sin, communicating with a sinful priest and yielding their obedience to the unjust and unlawful episcopacy of their leader, when the divine censure threatens through the prophet Hosea and says, "Their sacrifices shall be like the bread of mourning: all who eat them shall be defiled." [This] teaching obviously [shows] that all are indeed involved in sin who have been contaminated by the sacrifice of a blasphemous and unjust priest.

But when they are in Chaldea without a temple and without an altar, they will not pour out wine to the Lord, but to demons; and they will not please him, those who pour out to foreign gods, and who are held in captivity and among the Assyrians eat things sacrificed to idols, and are like the bread of mourners. For it is not lawful to eat of the sacrifices of mourners, and if anyone eats, what was offered becomes unclean. The Greeks call the suppers of mourners περίδειπνα; we can call them parentalia, from the fact that they are offered for dead parents. And not only he who has offered, but also he who has eaten of food of this kind will be unclean; for their bread, that is, the food which they offer, will not enter into the house of the Lord, which has been destroyed, which has been burned with Babylonian fire; but it will be for their own soul. And the sense is: they provide for their own gullet and their own pleasure; but polluted things do not please me.

9:5.t: What will you do on the solemn day, on the day of the festival of the Lord? For behold, they have set out from the devastation; Egypt will gather them, Memphis will bury them; the nettle will inherit the desirable things of their silver, the bur will be in their tents. LXX: What will you do on the day of assembly and on the day of the solemnity of the Lord? Therefore behold, they will go from the misery of Egypt, and Memphis will receive them, and Michmash will bury them; destruction will possess their silver, thorns will be in their tents. When the day of captivity comes, he says, and the most savage enemy falls upon you, what is my solemnity? What victim do I hold as propitious? That he avenges me on my enemies, and puts a limit to wrong, and scourges the impious sons. What then will you do on the day of the festival of the Lord? Answer. And while they are silent, he answers himself, or rather he beholds with divine eyes what they are going to do.

It is said also to the heretics: When the solemn day comes, what are you going to do? For solemn day Aquila has translated time. From which it is manifest that it does not mean a festal day, but the time of retribution; for at once there follows: The days of vengeance have come, the days of your retribution have come. Behold, you have been laid waste by many enemies: the Assyrians and the Chaldeans have slaughtered you, you have fled to the world, and have been made like the other nations; there Memphis will bury you, which is interpreted from the mouth; and the sense is: you will receive according to your blasphemies, and what you have spoken you will feel in your punishments; the desirable things, that is, the dogmas which you had composed for yourselves with crafty eloquence, which is what silver signifies, the nettle will possess, which will consume you with eternal burning; and the bur or thorn will be in your tents; for thorns spring up in the hands of those who have been made drunk with the Babylonian cup. […]

9:6.t: Behold, he says, when misery and devastation pressed upon them, and the Assyrian and the Chaldean were eager to bind them as captives, they fled to Egypt. There Memphis will bury them, which at that time was the metropolis of Egypt, before Alexandria, which was formerly called No, received both the greatness of a city and its name from Alexander of Macedon. But what is said in the Seventy: Michmash will bury them, is not found in the Hebrew; but rather mamad, which is called desirable. From which it is clear that they were deceived by the similarity of the letters daleth and chaph, and in place of mamad, which all have translated desirable, they thought it was Michmash, a city of Egypt. We can also take what is said: For behold, they have set out from the devastation; Egypt will gather them, Memphis will bury them, of the tribe of Judah; […]

9:7.t: The days of visitation have come, the days of retribution have come; know, Israel, that you are a foolish prophet, an insane spiritual man; because of the multitude of your iniquity, and the multitude of madness. LXX: The days of vengeance have come, the days of your retribution have come, and Israel will be afflicted like a raving prophet, a man who had the spirit; because of the multitude of your iniquities, your madness has been multiplied. In this place too there is the usual error: for where we have translated: know, Israel, that is, Israelites, and in the Hebrew is read iadau, the Seventy translated: and will be afflicted, taking the letter iod for vau, and reading res for daleth; of which the one means knowledge, the other affliction or malice. Therefore the days of visitation have come, of which he had said above: What will you do on the solemn day, on the day of the festival of the Lord? The days of retribution have come. […]

9:8.t: The watchman of Ephraim with my God, the prophet, has become a snare of ruin over all his ways; madness in the house of his God; they have sinned deeply, as in the days of Gibeah; he will remember their iniquity and will visit their sins. LXX: The watchman of Ephraim with God, a prophet; a crooked snare over all his ways; they contrived madness in the house of God; they have been corrupted according to the days of the hill; he will remember their iniquities; he will take vengeance upon their sins. God gave princes for this purpose, that they might correct the people when it transgressed, and draw it back to the right road. Whence he also says to Ezekiel: I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Therefore Jeroboam was given among the people as a watchman, and as a prophet with my God, that is, with God, who speaks these things to Hosea. But he, according to what is written above: You have become a snare to the watch and a net spread out over Tabor; […]

Searching the ancient histories, I cannot find that any have rent the Church and led peoples astray from the house of the Lord, except those who had been appointed by God as priests and prophets, that is, watchmen. These, then, are turned into a crooked snare, placing a stumbling block in all places, so that whoever enters by their ways falls, and cannot stand in Christ, and is drawn away by various errors and carried by crooked paths to the precipice. These are the watchmen of Ephraim, who have contrived madness in the house of the Lord, that is, in the Church, or in the holy Scriptures, interpreting them perversely, or at least in each one of the believers, who is most rightly named the house of God. Therefore they have been corrupted and have perished according to the days of the hill, when they spoke iniquity against the heights and went up on vain roofs. […]

9:9.t: We can also take the days of Gibeah as that time when, in place of God, they chose for themselves a king from the city of Gibeah, that is, Saul. And he says that they have now sinned much more greatly by choosing Jeroboam and worshiping idols than at the time when they chose Saul; for here idolatry too was joined to schism, but there the worship of God remained among the people. Therefore he will remember their iniquity, he who is now thought, because of his patience, to have forgotten, and he will visit their sins, and the wounds which have long festered.

9:10.t: Like grapes in the desert I found Israel; like the first fruits of the fig tree at its top I saw their fathers; but they went in to Baal-peor and were estranged unto confusion; and they became abominable like the things they loved. LXX: As a grape in the desert I found Israel, and as an early fig on the fig tree I saw their fathers; but they went in to Baal-peor, and were estranged unto confusion; and they became abominable like the beloved. For which in other copies we read: and the beloved became as abominable, which agrees better with the truth. When the whole world was a desert and did not have the knowledge of God, I found, he says, the people of Israel like a grape in the wilderness; and how he found it, he says: Like the first fruits of the fig tree, at its top I saw their fathers. Therefore the people was found in Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. And note the exactness of the language: the parents are seen, the people is found; […]

9:11.t: Ephraim, that is, the ten tribes, has flown away like a bird into captivity and has departed from its place. And he called it a bird to show its swift passage into Babylon. But if we read, like a bird their glory has flown away, we say this, that the help of God has departed from them and flown away. And what follows, from birth and from the womb and from conception, can be understood in two ways: that the glory which has flown away from Ephraim departs also from their birth and from their womb and from their conception, that is, it deserts their sons and abandons their descendants. Or at least we say that Israel had all his glory in his multitude, and in this he thought himself greater than Judah his brother, because he was set over ten tribes, the other over two.

But let us say according to tropology that Ephraim, that is, the heretics, has departed from the Church like a bird, and has all his glory in birth and in the womb and in conception, if they have begotten many sons, whom the Lord threatens, even if they have been reared, to be punished as well, and not by any other whatever, but by the Lord himself, since they have begotten sons of fornication; and a true woe will be upon them when God has departed from them. And at the same time he unfolds what Ephraim was: when he was in the Church, he says, he was beaten by the temptations of this world as Tyre is by the waves of the sea, and yet he could suffer nothing adverse, because he had the foundation of Christ, upon which a house that is built cannot be overthrown. But now he leads out his sons to the slayer, that is, to the devil. And he said finely: he leads out, that is, he makes them go outside from the Church. […]

9:12.t: Whence the Lord says that even if they rear their sons and gather together a multitude of children, they will be handed over to death; and then a true woe will fall upon them, when God has departed from them.

Ephraim has flown away like a bird; their glory from birth and from the womb and from conception. And even if they rear their sons, I will make them childless among men. But woe to them also when I depart from them. Ephraim, as I saw, was Tyre, founded in beauty; and Ephraim will lead out his sons to the slayer. LXX: Ephraim has flown away like a bird; their glory in birth and in travail and conception; for even if they have reared their sons, they will be without sons among men, for woe to them also; my flesh is from them. Ephraim, as I saw, has offered his sons for a capture; and Ephraim, to lead out his sons to slaughter. In this place the translators greatly disagree among themselves. For in the place where we said: woe to them when I depart from them, the Seventy and Theodotion translated: woe to them, my flesh is from them; and seeking the reason why there is such great variety, I seem to myself to have found this: My flesh is said in the Hebrew tongue basari; […]

9:13.t: And consequently he sets forth what Ephraim, who is now deserted, once was: so beautiful, he says, was he, and so walled about with the help of God, as Tyre is girded by the sea, or at least like a very hard crag which, fixed in the earth, scorns all storms and does not care about whirlwinds and winds. But he himself, that is, Ephraim, or Tyre, which was founded in the fullness of the sea, will lead out his sons to captivity. Many refer this section to the times of Hazael, who besieged Samaria and afflicted it with famine for a long time, so that the besieged thought it lighter to perish by the sword than by starvation.

9:14.t: Give them, O Lord; what will you give them? Give them a womb without children and dry breasts. LXX: likewise. If we wrongly abuse the things that God has given as a blessing, and they are turned to the opposite of the purpose for which they were given by him, it is expedient that they be taken away from us. Finally, the tongue was given for praising the Lord God and for speaking the things that are good. If anyone abuses it for blasphemy, against him the psalmist prays to the Lord: Let the deceitful lips be made dumb, which speak iniquity against the righteous in pride and in abuse. And in another place: May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips and the boastful tongue. Since, therefore, Ephraim gloried in the womb, and in conception, and in childbirth, and in the multitude of his peoples, the prophet prays to the Lord and says: Give them, O Lord. And he answers himself: What will you give them? […]

Their sheep are fruitful. They have many sons: for the number of heretics is great. Their sheep are fruitful. Whence it is said also in Hosea the prophet: Lord, give to them. What will you give them? A barren womb and dry breasts. About whom is this said? About the masters of the heretics, who applaud themselves in the number of their disciples.

9:15.t:
All their wickednesses are in Gilgal, for there I held them in hatred. LXX: likewise. In Gilgal Saul was anointed king, while Samuel announced the wrath of God to the people. There, he says, I held them in hatred, and by asking for a man as their king they withdrew from my rule. Or because Gilgal is a place of idolatry: there they committed all their crimes. But since Gilgal is interpreted revelation, or κυλισμοὶ, that is, wallowing-places, he says that all the wickedness of the heretics is to be revealed at that time when God gives them a barren womb and dry breasts, and they see their own shame. And those who boasted through pride that they had climbed to the heights will be rolled down to the earth, or dragged down to hell. Truly the heretics are worthy of God's hatred, who speak a lie against God, of whom he says in what follows:

Because of the malice of their devices I will cast them out of my house. There follows: I will not again love them; all their princes are departing, or disobedient. […]

9:16.t: Ephraim is stricken; their root is dried up; they will bear no fruit at all; and even if they beget, I will slay the most beloved of their womb. God will cast them away because they did not hear him; and they will be wanderers among the nations. LXX: Ephraim has suffered pain in his roots; he is withered, he bears no fruit at all; for even if they beget, I will slay the desirable things of their womb. God will reject them because they did not hear him; and they will be wanderers among the nations. He takes a metaphor from a tree, which, if its roots have withered, cannot bear fruit, and if it produces a little, will at once dry up in the very blossom. He speaks, moreover, of Ephraim, whose root has withered because he lost God, in whom he had been founded, or did not deserve to have his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, in whom he had sent down his root; and therefore he does not produce the fruit of righteousness; […]

10:1.t: Israel is a leafy vine, its fruit was made equal to it; according to the multitude of its fruit it multiplied altars, according to the richness of its land it abounded in images. LXX: Israel is a leafy vine, abundant fruit in it; according to the multitude of its fruits it multiplied altars, according to the good things of their land they will build monuments. For leafy vine, Aquila translated ἕνυδρον, which we can call watery, or ἔξίτηλον, because it loses the flavor of wine. Symmachus has ὑλομανοῦσαν, one that has grown entirely into leaves. Vines that have not been pruned by the vinedresser run riot into shoots and leaves, and the moisture that they ought to have changed into wine they squander on the empty ambition of foliage and leaves; a vine of this kind is ruinous to farmers. Such was Israel, growing in the multitude of its peoples, and not rendering fruit to God the farmer. […]

In Scripture there is first a fixing of the roots of virtue, as in the Patriarchs. But later, in the establishment of commands and sacrifices, there is a production of green foliage. Hence, in Hosea, "Israel is a luxuriant vine." And because foliage is not to last forever, but is to be followed by flowers, there followed prophecy with both fragrance and beauty.

10:2.t: Their heart is divided; now they will perish, he himself will break their images, he will lay waste their altars. LXX: They have divided their hearts; now they will perish; he himself will dig under their altars; their monuments will be afflicted. The Hebrews hand down a tale of this kind, confirming their surmise by the authority of the Scriptures: as long as both the kings and the people alike worshiped the golden calves and were in agreement in impiety, captivity did not come. The last king of the ten tribes was Hoshea, of whom it is written that he did indeed do evil in the sight of the Lord, but not like the kings of Israel who were before him; in whose ninth year Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, took the people of Israel, and led them away to the Assyrians, and made them dwell by the river Gozan in the cities of the Medes. It is asked, therefore, why they were not taken captive under the worst kings, but under one who had begun in some part to turn to better things? […]

10:3.t: For now they will say: We have no king; for we do not fear the Lord, and what will a king do for us? Speak words of a useless vision, and you will strike a covenant, and judgment will spring up like bitterness over the furrows of the field. LXX: Therefore now they will say: We have no king, because we did not fear the Lord, but what will a king do for us? Speaking words, lying pretexts; he will draw up a testament, judgment will spring up like grass upon the wilderness of the field. After God has broken the images of Israel, and laid waste their altars or statues, and the final captivity has come, they will say: We have no king. And lest they think that the sentence is put off for a long time, he added: Now they will say, when they are laid waste, when they perceive that Hoshea, their last king, has been taken from them; but the king has been taken from us for this reason, because we did not fear the Lord, the true king; for what could a man as king profit us?

The disciples of contrary dogmas too, when their lies have been crushed and their altars and groves overthrown, will say too late: We do not have the kings who formerly ruled over us, by whose deceptions we did not fear the Lord; for what did it profit us to follow those whose help we do not feel in our need? They will say these things seeking some excuse, so that they may seem to have erred not through themselves but through very bad teachers. Hence also the LXX translated their words as false excuses, which the prophet shuns, saying: Do not incline my heart to words of malice, to make excuses in sins. We gladly applaud our own vices, and, overcome by pleasures, we plead the weakness of the flesh or the harsh commands of our elders; hence the words and visions of the heretics will be useless. And they will strike a covenant, not at all with God, but with bitterness, which, when the day of judgment has come, will spring up over the furrows of their field; so that those who sowed in joy may reap in tears; […]

10:4.t: Say what you will, sigh after your old errors, promise yourselves prosperity, which will be turned into its opposite; you will strike a covenant, not at all with God, but with a lie. And after the covenant, which the Seventy translated testament, there will spring up for you not a fruitful crop of grain, not even barley, the food of beasts of burden, not various pulses, not vines that sweat out their fruit into must; the trees will not put forth fruits that change the moisture of the earth into various flavors; but bitterness will spring up for you, or rather the judgment of bitterness, or ἄγρωστις, which in Latin we render as grass. For it is a kind of plant like a reed, which at each of its joints sends a shoot upward and a root downward, and these shoots and twigs in turn are the seedbeds of another plant, and so in a short time, unless it is dug out to its deepest roots, it makes whole fields like thickets of briars. […]

For that the message of salvation would take possession of the whole world, the God of all declared by one of the holy prophets, saying of it, "Judgment springeth up like couch-grass in the furrows of the field." For like as the couch-grass springs up in the furrows that are left without cultivation, and takes possession of them, and spreads everywhere, constantly advancing onwards, so in an exactly similar manner has judgment, that is to say, the grace that justifieth the world as declared in the saving tidings of the Gospel, taken possession of every city and place.
10:4.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

10:5.t: And the expression, "They opened their mouth upon me like a roaring lion," designates him who was then king of the Jews, and was called Herod, a successor of the Herod who, when Christ was born, slew all the infants in Bethlehem born about the same time, because he imagined that amongst them He would assuredly be of whom the Magi from Arabia had spoken; for he was ignorant of the will of Him that is stronger than all, how He had commanded Joseph and Mary to take the Child and depart into Egypt, and there to remain until a revelation should again be made to them to return into their own country. And there they did remain until Herod, who slew the infants in Bethlehem, was dead, and Archelaus had succeeded him. And he died before Christ came to the dispensation on the cross which was given Him by His Father. And when Herod succeeded Archelaus, having received the authority which had been allotted to him, Pilate sent to him by way of compliment Jesus bound; […]

The Lord himself comes to a trial with "the elders and rulers of the people," as Isaiah predicted. And then he fulfilled all that had been written of his passion. At that time "the heathen raged, and the people imagined vain things; the kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers gathered themselves together against the Lord and against his Christ." The heathen were Pilate and the Romans; the people were the tribes of Israel; the kings were represented in Herod and the rulers in the chief priests. When, indeed, he was sent to Herod gratuitously by Pilate, the words of Hosea were accomplished, for he had prophesied of Christ, "And they shall carry him bound as a present to the king."

The inhabitants of Samaria worshiped the cows of Beth-aven, for its people mourned over it; and its temple-keepers exulted over it in its glory, because it departed from it. For indeed it too was carried into Assyria, a gift to the avenging king; shame will seize Ephraim; Israel will be put to shame in his own will. LXX: With the calf of the house of ὢν those who dwell in Samaria will sojourn, for its people mourned over it. And as they provoked him, they will rejoice over its glory, because it was carried away from it; and binding it for the Assyrians, they bore gifts to King Jareb in the house. Ephraim will receive shame, Israel will be put to shame in his own counsel. What Beth-aven is, for which the LXX translated house of ὢν, and who King Jareb is, which is interpreted avenger, we have discussed more fully above. In Beth-aven, then, that is, Bethel, the inhabitants of Samaria worshiped the golden cows; […]

According to the spiritual understanding we must labor at how we may fit everything to the heretics. The cows of Beth-aven, or of the house of ὢν, which is interpreted toil, were worshiped by the heretics, who boasted that they dwelt in the keeping of the commandments of God, that is, in Samaria; and on the day of judgment, when judgment will spring up like bitterness upon the furrows of the field, the people will mourn over it, that is, over the calf, and over the perverse dogma which it thought to be God. But of the temple-keepers too he did not say, will exult, but, exulted, referring it to past time, over their glory, with which they had once fabricated their glorious things, because the people had departed from God, or because the very glory of God had departed from the people, by whom it had been abandoned.

10:6.t: And that we may know, they say, that this is what is meant, the following verse shows it clearly: For indeed it was carried into Assyria, a gift to the avenging king. And at once there follows: Shame will seize Ephraim, and Israel will be put to shame in his own will, or in his own counsel. For the fraud of the gilded calves, once detected, is reported to the king of Israel by letter, and the very thing by which they had thought to please is that by which they are put to shame most of all; and they offend those to whom they had sent the gifts, who think that this was accomplished not by the theft of the priests but by the fraud and counsel of the kings. We read in the book of Kings that Menahem, king of Israel, sent to Pul, king of the Assyrians, a thousand talents of silver, that his hand might be with him, that is, that he might give him help; and some think that among these the golden calves too were carried off. […]

And whatever the heretics say and compose in fine language, they send as gifts to their king, the devil, referring everything to him; whence shame will seize them for ever, and they will be put to shame in their own wills. A certain man has left it written in his commentaries, both above and in the present place, that King Jareb, that is, the avenger, is to be understood as Christ. This displeases us altogether. For it is impious that what according to the history will be understood of the Assyrian king should according to tropology be referred to Christ.

10:7.t: But the Samaria of spiritual wickedness too, which had divided itself from the people of God, made its king pass swiftly away, namely the speech of the heretics and their doctrine, like foam, or brushwood, upon the face of the water: the one, even while it is seen, suddenly dissolves; the other is easy to lift from the surface of the waters and cast into the fire. Such are the heretics, swelling with foaming words and mixing precepts destined for burning into the baptism of Christ and into his words.

Samaria has made her king pass away like foam upon the face of the water, and the high places of the idol, the sin of Israel, will be destroyed. The bur and the thistle will come up upon their altars; and they will say to the mountains: Cover us; and to the hills: Fall upon us. LXX: Samaria has cast out her king like brushwood upon the face of the water, and the altars of ὦν, the sins of Israel, will be taken away. Thorns and thistles will come up upon their altars; and they will say to the mountains: Cover us; and to the hills: Fall upon us. For foam, which the LXX and Theodotion translated φρύγανον, that is, brushwood, dry grasses and withered twigs, which are got ready for the furnace and for burning, Symmachus put ἐπίζεμα, wishing to indicate the upper waters of a boiling pot, rising into foam and bubbles, which the Greeks call πομφόλυγας. As, then, the foam that is upon the water quickly dissolves, so the kingdom of the ten tribes will swiftly be ended; […]

10:8.t: But once the idol and its high places have been scattered: The bur and the thistle will come up upon their altars. A sign of utter desolation, so that not even walls and the last traces of buildings are left. At that time they will say to the mountains: Cover us; and to the hills: Fall upon us. This the Lord says is to be fulfilled in the last time of the Jewish captivity. Whatever, then, is now said against the ten tribes, or against all Israel, let us know that it can also be transferred τυπικώς (typologically) to the whole people, so that when the Romans had taken Jerusalem and overthrown the temple, or when the day of judgment comes, as others suppose, they say, fearing with great horror, to the mountains: Cover us; and to the hills: Fall upon us, preferring to die rather than to see the things that bring death.

All these will pass away, and the grand words on which they labored, which is what ὦν is interpreted, will at once be scattered, the words in which Israel sinned; and so great will be the desolation of that most wicked doctrine that thorns and thistles will come up upon their altars. That thorns and thistles spring up where there is no cultivation of the fields is plain to all. These are the thorns that choke the seed and do not let it grow, which spring up in the hand of the drunkard, and which Israel produced instead of the grape. For the Lord waited for it to produce grapes, and it produced thorns, or the wild vine, which has the likeness of the grape and twists the mouths of those who eat it with its bitter taste. Therefore, when the time of judgment comes and all things have been overthrown, they will say to the mountains, which they formerly thought lofty, and to their former teachers: Cover us; and to the hills: Fall upon us. […]

10:9.t: The Seventy interpreted Gibeah as hills. From the days of the hills, then, Israel has sinned, when it abandoned the mountains of the Church and went down to the hills, or heretical slopes, thinking itself more learned than the Church is and to have found something more sublime: there they stood, that is, they persisted in error. And what follows, The battle will not overtake them on the hill, some have interpreted thus: because they have begotten sons of iniquity, and, withdrawing from the Church, have begun to be on the hills, when persecution comes the battle will not overtake them, since the devil is unwilling to attack his own. Others thus: Since from the days of the hills Israel has sinned, and stood there and could walk no further, must it not be overtaken by battle on the hills? Ought not churchmen to fight against it, to destroy them over the sons of iniquity? If they are overtaken and overcome, they will no longer be able to beget.

From the days of Gibeah Israel has sinned; there they stood. The battle against the sons of iniquity will not overtake them in Gibeah. According to my desire I will chastise them; peoples will be gathered against them when they are chastised for their two iniquities. LXX: Since the hills have been, Israel has sinned; there they stood. War did not overtake them on the hill against the sons of iniquity; he came to chastise them, and peoples will be gathered against them when they have been chastised in their two iniquities. From the day on which Benjamin shamefully and cruelly killed the Levite's wife in the city of Gibeah, all Israel has sinned against me; not because it avenged the wrong and punished the crime with blood, but because it leapt to battle out of a husband's grief and would not avenge the sacrilege against its own God, in that it disregarded the ephod and teraphim in the house of Micah, which were worshiped as idols. Here, then, Israel stood; […]

10:10.t: And at the same time the Lord promises that he will chastise and instruct them, so that, when the teachers have been overcome, their own disciples, whom they had deceived before, may be gathered against them and see the chastisement on account of the two iniquities: because they both abandoned the Church, the fountain of the Lord, and dug for themselves broken cisterns, namely the caves of the heretics, which cannot hold the waters, that is, the doctrine of the Savior and the mystery of baptism.

10:11.t: Ephraim is a heifer trained to love threshing, and I passed over the beauty of her neck; and I will mount upon Ephraim; Judah will plow, Jacob will break up the furrows for himself. LXX: Ephraim is a heifer — or a cow; for what in Hebrew is called egla, that is, μόσχος (calf) and δάμαλις (heifer), signifies both —; Ephraim, then, is a heifer taught to love contention; but I will come upon the beauty of her neck; I will lay upon Ephraim and I will keep silent about Judah; Jacob will be strengthened for himself. This passage, or rather everything that follows this section, is wrapped in great obscurities. Hence let both we who try to explain it and the prudent reader with us pay attention, so that, if not the truth, which is most difficult, we may at least be able to track down a conjecture of what is probable. The divine word has this custom, to express the truth of the history through tropology and metaphor. […]

10:12.t: But behold also how holy and how wonderful is the very order of the things. Not first the "breastpiece" and afterward the "ephod", because wisdom is not before works, but works ought first to be had and afterward wisdom is to be sought. Then, next, not "manifestation" before the "rational", because we ought not to teach others before we ourselves are instructed and rational. But above these is added "truth", because "truth" is the highest wisdom. Finally the prophet too keeps this same order, when he says: "Sow for yourselves unto righteousness, and reap the fruit of life, kindle for yourselves the light of knowledge." You see how he does not say first: "Kindle for yourselves the light of knowledge", but first: "Sow for yourselves unto righteousness", and it does not suffice to sow, but "reap," he says, "the fruit of life", so that after these things you may be able to fulfill what follows: "Kindle for yourselves the light of knowledge."

And furthermore the Prophet Hosea also said:—Light you a lamp and seek ye the Lord. And our Lord Jesus Christ said:—What woman is there who has ten drachmos and shall lose one of them, and will not light a lamp and sweep the house and seek her drachma that she lost? What then does this woman signify? Clearly the congregation of the house of Israel, to which the ten commandments were given. They lost the first commandment—that in which He warned them saying:—I am the Lord your God, Who brought you up from the land of Egypt. And when they had lost this first commandment, also the nine which are after it they could not keep, because on the first depend the nine. For it was an impossibility that while worshipping Baal, they should keep the nine commandments. For they lost the first commandment, like that woman who lost one drachma from the ten. So the Prophet cried unto them:—Light you a lamp and seek ye the Lord. […]

But such are they, and in this condition; but let us kindle for ourselves the light of knowledge. This will be done by sowing unto righteousness, and reaping the fruit of life, for action is the patron of contemplation, that amongst other things we may learn also what is the true light, and what the false, and be saved from falling unawares into evil wearing the guise of good.

Sow for yourselves in righteousness and reap in the mouth of mercy. Renew for yourselves the fallow ground; but it is the time of seeking the Lord, when he comes who will teach you righteousness. LXX: Sow for yourselves in righteousness, gather for yourselves the vintage of the fruit of life; light for yourselves the light of knowledge, for it is time; seek the Lord, until the fruits of righteousness come to you. He keeps up the metaphor taken from farmers, once he has begun it. He had said that Ephraim, a trained heifer, loves and cherishes the threshing of the threshing floor, and that he had mounted upon her neck, and that Judah had plowed, and that Jacob had broken up the furrows, or the clods. Now he commands them to sow for themselves through repentance, and to sow in righteousness, that is, in the law, and to reap in mercy, that is, in the grace of the Gospel; for there it is: An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth; here we read: Whoever strikes you on the right cheek, offer him the other as well. […]

And beautifully does God give to the good man wisdom and knowledge and joy: for unless he has been good and has first corrected his ways by his own free choice, he does not deserve wisdom and knowledge and joy, according to what is said elsewhere: Sow for yourselves in righteousness, gather the vintage in the fruit of life, light for yourselves the light of knowledge. For righteousness must first be sown, and the fruit of life reaped, and afterwards the light of knowledge will be able to appear.

There is then no way of arriving at spiritual knowledge but this which one of the prophets has finely described: "Sow to yourselves for righteousness: reap the hope of life. Enlighten yourselves with the light of knowledge." First then we must sow for righteousness, i.e., by works of righteousness we must extend practical perfection; next we must reap the hope of life, i.e., by the expulsion of carnal sins must gather the fruits of spiritual virtues: and so we shall succeed in enlightening ourselves with the light of knowledge. And the Psalmist also sees that this system ought to be followed, when he says: "Blessed are they that are undefiled in the way: who walk in the law of the Lord. Blessed are they that seek His testimonies." For he does not say in the first place: "Blessed are they that seek His testimonies, and afterwards add: Blessed are they that are undefiled in the way;" but he begins by saying: "Blessed are they that are undefiled in the way;" […]
10:12.s: The First Conference of Abbot Nesteros, Chapter 16

10:12.t: I do not say, however, that knowledge of letters is to be despised or neglected, which adorns the soul and instructs it, and makes it able to instruct others also. But those two things ought and are expedient to come first, in which the preceding argument declared the sum of salvation to consist. And see whether he was not contemplating and teaching this order who said: Sow for yourselves unto justice, reap the hope of life; and then at last, he says, illuminate for yourselves the light of knowledge. He placed knowledge last, as a painting, which cannot stand upon an empty surface; and therefore he set those two things before it and placed them beneath it, as if he were laying something solid beneath a painting. I shall now attend to knowledge in safety, if first through the benefit of hope I shall have received security of life. […]
10:12.s: Sermons on the Song of Songs, Sermon 37

10:13.t: You have ploughed impiety, you have reaped iniquity; you have eaten the fruit of lying. LXX: Why do you keep silent about impieties, and you have gathered the vintage of his iniquities; you have eaten lying fruit. I am compelled against my will to discuss rather often the peculiarities of the Hebrew language; for we do not, after the manner of the rhetoricians, repeat maxims, build up words, and rouse our hearers or readers by declamations to our own praises. But what is obscure, above all in a foreign tongue, we strive to explain to men. Above, where we translated: Judah shall plough, in the Hebrew is read ieros, with iod as the first letter; the Seventy, thinking it uau, translated: and shall I keep silent? Now too in the Hebrew is written arasthem, which we have rendered you have ploughed, for which the Seventy translated: why do you keep silent; by the same error as above, rendering silence for ploughing. […]

Because you have trusted in your ways, in the multitude of your mighty men,

a tumult will rise up among your people, and all your fortresses will be laid waste; as Salmana was laid waste by the house of him who judged Baal in the day of battle, the mother dashed down upon the sons, so has Bethel done to you from the face of the malice of your wickednesses. LXX: Because you have hoped in your chariots, in the multitude of your strength, destruction will rise up among your people, and all your walled places will depart; as the princes of Salmana from the house of Jerubbaal in the days of war dashed the mother down upon the sons, so will I do to you, house of Israel, from the face of your wickednesses. Therefore you have eaten the fruit of lying, and in all that you set before yourselves an empty hope has deceived you; because you have trusted, O Ephraim, in the ways of your idolatry; for these are your ways; and in the multitude of your mighty men, having your hope not in God but in the strength of an army.

We have escaped, after a fashion, from the rugged places; now, spreading our sails for the deep, let us cross the sea of allegory. Because you have trusted, O Ephraim, in the ways, or in the chariots, of yours, of which it is written: Some in chariots and some in horses; but we will be magnified in the name of the Lord our God; and you have trusted in the multitude of your mighty men, whom you have strengthened for yourself by false knowledge; therefore a tumult and noise will rise up among your people. For whatever the heretics say has no voice that unfolds meanings, but only tumult, clamor and noise. And all your fortresses, or the things that are walled, will be laid waste —, for they have been fortified and built not with the testimonies of the Scriptures, but with the art of dialectic and the arguments of the philosophers —; as Salmana was once laid waste by Gideon, the mother being killed upon her sons. […]

10:14.t: And if any prefer to apply the prophecy to the people, regarding it as spoken concerning the people of Israel, let him consider the sequence of the argument, which implies that this will take place after the saying addressed as to Jerusalem itself, "And destruction shall be raised up in thy people, and all thy strong places shall depart." And those things, it says, which such and such a king suffered in a war in which he was involved, when they dashed the mother to the ground on her children, the like will I do unto you because of your wickedness. He must mean by "you" them that are called Israelites, who also were cast away with their king, by whom he implies Herod. "And you have suffered all this," it says, "because Israel is a child, and I loved him, and out of Egypt have I called my son." But how can he praise and blame the same people at the same time? The real meaning supplies the explanation. The Christ is called "Israel," in other prophecies, as He is in this. […]
10:14.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 9, Chapter 4

10:14.t: And so a tumult will rise up among your people, which in Hebrew is called Saon, that is, the noise and roaring of a howling army; and at their shouting all your fortresses will be laid waste; and the places you thought fortified and safe will lie open to the enemy and will be laid waste just as Salmana, the prince of the Midianites, was laid waste and crushed, who was killed by the house of Jerubbaal. There is no doubt that he means Gideon, who, from the fact that he destroyed the temple of Baal and cut down the grove, and Baal could not avenge himself, obtained the surname Jerubbaal, that is, let Baal avenge himself; so that, as Salmana killed the sons in front of their mothers, the mothers themselves also being killed afterwards, so too your sons, O Ephraim, may be killed in your presence, you who are yourself also to be slaughtered. We ask where it is written that Salmana killed the mother upon her sons; […]

As, therefore, Salmana was laid waste by Jerubbaal, whom some wrongly think to be Jeroboam son of Nebat, who ruled over the ten tribes, and was laid waste, as is contained in the Hebrew, by Arbel, which signifies the very same thing as Jerubbaal, but in a shorter and more eloquent expression; so has Bethel done to you, O Israel, from the face of your wickednesses, Bethel, where you set up the golden calf and worshipped the gods of Egypt. For Bethel, which is interpreted house of God, the LXX translated house of Israel, which is not found at all in the Hebrew.

10:15.t: And what follows, So has Bethel done to you from the face of the malice of your wickednesses, is properly fitted to the leaders of the heretics: that Bethel has done this to them, the one they themselves call Bethel, that is, the house of God, and a false Church; so that the sense is: So will your Church do to you, which you call the house of God; but from the time it is held by you, it must be called Beth-aven, that is, house of the idol, because of the multitude of your wickednesses.

As the morning passes, the king of Israel has passed away; because Israel was a child, and I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son; they called them, so they went away from their face. They sacrificed to the Baalim and offered sacrifice to images. LXX: In the morning they were cast away, the king of Israel was cast away; because Israel was a little child, and I loved him, and out of Egypt I called his sons. As I called them, so they themselves went away from my face. They sacrificed to the Baalim and burned incense to carved images. He sets out the same sense under different figures. He who had said above: Samaria has made her king pass away like foam upon the face of the water, because foam and bubbles floating on the surface of the waters are quickly dissolved, now puts the same thing under another likeness. […]

And we understand that the heretics pass away like the first light of dawn, and their king, the devil, or the heresiarch; whom in their infancy, — when they believed in the Church, and were little ones, and were reckoned under the name of Christ —, God loved; and he called them out of the tribulation and darkness of Egypt. And he called them through the apostles and the teachers of the Church. And when they had been called, he says, by my leaders, they withdrew from their face and worshipped Baal-peor, that is, they served their own vices and lust, and afterwards they sacrificed to the Baalim and to images which they had fashioned for themselves. For each of the heretics has his own gods, and whatever they have feigned they set up as a carved and a molten image.

11:1.t:
[Passages quoted, Hos. x. 14; xi. 1.]

FOLLOWING the Hebrew slavishly, Aquila translates, "Out of Egypt have I called my son." But I have noted the exact words, because Matthew quoted the prophecy, when he recorded that Jesus was carried into Egypt, and returned thence to the land of Israel. And if any one objects to the idea of our Saviour's going into Egypt, let him know that He went for good reasons. For neither was it fitting for Him to restrain Herod from his self-chosen wickedness, nor that our Saviour while still an infant should begin to shew His Divine Power by working miracles before the time, which would have been the case, if He had punished Herod miraculously for plotting against Him, and had not submitted to go down to Egypt with His parents. […]
11:1.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 9, Chapter 4

11:1.t: I will address myself as is right to those who have come from Egypt; for they have come here eagerly, having overcome illwill by zeal, from that Egypt which is enriched by the River, raining out of the earth, and like the sea in its season,—if I too may follow in my small measure those who have so eloquently spoken of these matters; and which is also enriched by Christ my Lord, Who once was a fugitive into Egypt, and now is supplied by Egypt; the first, when He fled from Herod's massacre of the children; and now by the love of the fathers for their children, by Christ the new Food of those who hunger after good; the greatest alms of corn of which history speaks and men believe; the Bread which came down from heaven and giveth life to the world, that life which is indestructible and indissoluble, concerning Whom I now seem to hear the Father saying, Out of Egypt have I called My Son.

That what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: Out of Egypt I have called my son. Let those who deny the truth of the Hebrew volumes answer where this is read in the LXX translators. And when they have not found it, we shall tell them that it is written in the prophet Hosea, as the copies too can prove which we have lately published. But we can also relieve this passage in another way, for the sake of the contentious, whose custom the apostle Paul denies that he or the Church of Christ has; and we bring forward a testimony from Numbers, where Balaam says: God has called him out of Egypt, his glory is like that of the unicorn.

And he sets out the benefits that God conferred upon him. While he was a boy, he says, and a little child, and was held captive in Egypt, I loved him so much that I sent my servant Moses, and called out of Egypt my son, of whom I said in another place: Israel is my firstborn son.

Where we have said: Out of Egypt I called my son, the Seventy translated: Out of Egypt I called his sons, which is not found in the Hebrew; and no one doubts that Matthew took his testimony from this place according to the Hebrew truth. Therefore let those who disparage our translation produce the scripture from which the evangelist took this testimony and interpreted it of the Lord Savior, when he was brought back from Egypt into the land of Israel. And when they cannot find it, let them stop wrinkling the forehead, knitting the brow, curling the nose and snapping their fingers. The emperor Julian, in the seventh volume of what he vomited forth against us, that is, against the Christians, slanders this place, and says that what was written of Israel the evangelist Matthew transferred to Christ in order to mock the simplicity of those of the Gentiles who had believed. To him we will answer briefly: first, that Matthew published his Gospel in Hebrew letters, which none could read except those who were of the Hebrews. […]

11:2.t: And because Israel is indeed spoken of in the singular but understood in the plural, as are people, Ephraim and Judah, since in the singular number there is a great number contained in this number, he recalls the old history: that he called them through Moses and Aaron, who called them to go out of Egypt; but they, called by them, withdrew from their face, turning their backs on him and showing the hardness of their mind by the gesture of their body. Nor was it enough for them to despise those who called them, unless they also sacrificed to Baal and burned incense to carved images, or idols. We read that they first worshipped Baal under Ahab king of Israel, who took as his wife Jezebel, daughter of the king of Sidon, and brought the Babylonian and Phoenician idol over into Samaria. […]

11:3.t: And I was like a foster-father to Ephraim, I carried them in my arms, and they did not know that I was healing them. With the cords of Adam I will draw them, with the bonds of love. And I will be to them as one who lifts the yoke upon their jaws, and I inclined toward him that he might eat. LXX: And I bound Ephraim together, I took him up upon my arm; and they did not know that I was healing them in the corruption of men; I stretched them out in the bonds of my love. And I will be to them as a man giving slaps upon his jaws; and I will look upon him, prevailing over him. The Hebrew and the edition of the Seventy translators differ greatly from each other. Let us try, therefore, to weave the history according to the Hebrews, and ἀναγωγὴν (anagogy) according to the LXX. […]

Let us pass to the spiritual understanding, according to the Seventy translators only; lest, if we wish to expound both, according to the history and according to ἀναγωγὴν, we stretch out the size of the book. While they sacrificed to the Baalim which they had fashioned from their own heart, and, when I called, fled from my face, — for so it stands in the Seventy —, I, the most merciful Lord, bound the feet of Ephraim, that they might not flee farther from me; for this is what συνεπόδισα signifies. And I bound them with the testimonies of the Scriptures and the disputation of the teachers of the Church, so that he might hold them, bound through patience, in his arms, while they did not understand that the patience of God was the occasion of their salvation.

Otherwise: I loved them so much, and was so merciful a shepherd, that I myself carried the sick sheep on my shoulders; but they did not know that I was healing them by my passion, and that I, who am the lover of all men, was drawing them to believe with the bonds of love, according to what is written in the Gospel: No one comes to me unless the Father who sent me draws him. And they thought my light yoke most heavy; and I inclined toward them, leaving the kingdoms of the heavens, so as to eat with them, having taken the form of a man; or I gave them my body to eat, I myself both the food and the guest at table.

11:4.t: And I healed them because of the cords and bonds of love with which I had bound Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to myself. For in place of Adam, Aquila and Symmachus and the Seventy and Theodotion translated all men, so as to say: with the cords of men I will draw them, with the bonds of love. And what follows, I will be to them as one who lifts the yoke, for which Symmachus translated: and they thought that I was putting a yoke upon their jaw, is taken in two ways: either I took from them the yoke of all the nations round about, or they thought my law a most heavy weight of a yoke. And I gave him manna as food in the desert, for him to eat; for this is what he says: and I inclined toward him that he might eat; for which Symmachus translated: and I inclined food toward him. Not that God inclined toward him, but that he made the food of manna incline toward him.

Hence, in the corruption of men, that is, of the teachers who had deceived them, I extended the warmth of faith to those contracted by the cold of faithlessness, and bound them, resisting as they were, with the bonds of my love. And because they did not run of their own accord, but were dragged along bound with ropes, I struck their jaws a little with slaps, not punishing but correcting and amending. A judge tears the flesh, tortures with cords, torments with scourges and fire. But he who is a father strikes his wanton son with the palm of the hand. And he finely did not say: I will be beating them with slaps, but: as a man striking the jaws with the hand. And God strikes his straying sons with the threat of punishments, with the reading of the Gospel and the testimonies of the prophets. And when he has so struck on the jaw as to knock the bread and doctrine of the heretics out of the polluted mouth, then he looks upon him, while the beaten son says to him: Look upon me and have mercy on me. […]

11:5.t: He will not return into the land of Egypt, and Assyria itself is his king, because they would not be converted. The sword has begun in his cities and will consume his chosen ones; and it will eat their heads, and my people will hang in suspense for my return. But a yoke will be laid upon them all together, which will not be taken away. LXX: Ephraim will dwell in Egypt, and Assyria itself is his king, because he would not be converted. And the sword has grown weak in his cities, and has rested in his hands, and they will eat of their own thoughts; and his people hangs from its sojourning, and God will be angry over his precious things, and will not exalt him. When he says: he will not return into the land of Egypt, he shows that he desires to return but cannot go. For Israel desired to return, begging for help from the Egyptians; but he was taken in possession by the Assyrian, who captured him and ruled over him by the right of the victor; and he suffered this because he would not be converted nor repent. […]

According to the Seventy, Ephraim dwelt in Egypt, saying that he held the holy land and the Church of the Lord Savior; but by vices and sins and the perversity of his faith he always lingered in Egypt. Because, therefore, he dwelt in Egypt, the great mind, the Assyrian, will be his king; for he would not return to the Church, and, having lost power, that is, Christ, who is the power of God and the wisdom of God, he has always lived in languor; and he was weak, subject to all the demons and passions; therefore the sword, that is, spiritual knowledge or the word of a churchman, laying waste and subduing, will always be at work in his cities, which he impiously built against God; and the sword itself will rest in his hands, so that, slain by another, he cannot slay another nor lift his hand against the adversary. Finally they will receive, and will devour, according to their own counsels.

11:6.t: And so the sword has begun in his cities, or will rush in, as Aquila translated, or will wound, as Symmachus rendered. And see how great is the weight of miseries: not that fields or possessions and the countryside are laid waste, but that the enemy enters the midst of the cities and consumes his chosen ones, or his arms, as Symmachus translated, which in Hebrew is called baddau. And when the sword has consumed the chosen and the princes, or the strength of the army, and has devoured either their heads or their counsels, so that they can find no protection at all, then the wretched common people, who would not return to me, will wait for my return to them. And they will repent late, while the enemies lay everything waste. […]

11:7.t: But the unhappy people and the untaught crowd will sigh for their ancient homeland and will feel themselves to be captive, or will hang in suspense in their sojourning, not knowing what to do and ignorant where to turn. And God is angry over their precious things, namely the gold and silver which they had received from him, of which we have often spoken, and he will by no means set free him who has fallen by his own fault. This according to the LXX; and we will fit the same sense to the Hebrew as well.

11:8.t: How shall I give you up, Ephraim, shall I protect you, Israel? How shall I give you up like Admah, set you as Zeboiim? My heart is turned within me, my repentance is troubled together. I will not execute the fury of my wrath, I will not turn to destroy Ephraim, because I am God and not man; the Holy One in your midst, and I will not enter the city. LXX: What shall I do to you, Ephraim, shall I protect you, Israel? What shall I do to you? I will set you as Admah and as Zeboiim; my heart is turned in him; my repentance is troubled together. I will not act according to the wrath of my fury. I will not abandon Ephraim to be destroyed, because I am God, and not man; holy in you, and I will not enter the city. In that place where we and the LXX translated: shall I protect you, Israel? in the Hebrew is written amaggenach, which Aquila translated ὅπλῳ κυκλώσω σε, that is: I will surround you with a shield. […]

But if we wish to read: How shall I give you up, Ephraim, shall I protect you, Israel? it is to be understood thus: What shall I do to you? Are you worthy of protection, you who have done such things? It must also be noted that where something is said against Judah, that is, the people of God, it is not Admah and Zeboiim that are set down, but Sodom and Gomorrah. For we read in Isaiah: Hear the law of God, you princes of Sodom; and: Give heed to the word of the Lord, you people of Gomorrah. In the Gospel too, of the city which has not received the apostles, when they shake off the dust of their feet, it is said that in the day of judgment it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah than for that city. And the prophetic word is directed to Jerusalem: Sodom has been justified by you. We are therefore given ground to suspect that Sodom and Gomorrah were the leaders in sin, and that Admah and Zeboiim followed their example; because the mighty will suffer torments mightily; […]

To the heretics also, and to the people deceived by them, the Lord says that unless they repent they will be set as Admah and Zeboiim, so as to have no hope of salvation. Again, as a most merciful father, he says that he changes his sentence and repents of having said such things, so as to call them too to conversion and to repentance. I will not act, he says, in my fury, I will not destroy Ephraim. As far, he says, as lies in me, as far as I desire, if he corrects his error by the truth, if he loves me more than the leaders of heresy; God, indeed, am I, and not man: I will stretch out my hand to the fallen, I will call the wandering to salvation. And because I am holy, for that reason I will not enter the city, that is, the conventicles and cities of the heretics. Those who go out of their cities I gladly receive; into their cities I will not enter.

11:9.t:
[Passage quoted, Hos. xi. 9.]

IN these words God the Word says when He has become man to those who confess Him to be a holy man, but not God: "I am God and not a holy man among you." And, then, having called Himself God, He shews the Almighty Lord and God, His Father, adding: "I will go behind the Lord." And the words: "I will not enter into the city," are of one who refuses to take part in the common and vulgar life of men, from which also He dissuades his own disciples: "Go not on a road of the Gentiles, and enter not into a city of the Samaritans."
11:9.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 5, Chapter 22

11:9.t: I repented of destroying for ever my people of old; therefore I will not act according to the fury of my anger, nor will I be changed from my clemency so as to destroy Ephraim. For I do not strike in order to destroy for ever, but in order to amend. My cruelty is the occasion of repentance and of mercy. God, indeed, am I, and not man. Man punishes for this end, that he may destroy; God chastises for this end, that he may amend. The Holy One in your midst, and I will not enter the city, that is: I am not one of those who dwell in cities, who live by human laws, who think cruelty to be justice, for whom the highest law is the highest malice; but my law and my justice is to save those who have been corrected. We can also say otherwise: since Cain the parricide first built a city in the name of his son Enoch, the Lord does not enter a city of this kind, which was built by crime and blood and parricide.

This which he said, I will not enter the city, and what follows according to the LXX, I will walk after the Lord, some have interpreted so as to say that the people answered the Lord, and that the sense is: Because your heart is turned within you, and you have not dealt with us according to our sins, but imitate your own clemency, and do not punish our offenses, and promise that you, holy and merciful, will dwell in our midst, therefore I too will not enter the city of evil men, nor will I be of the number of sinners; but I will walk after the Lord our God. The Hebrews, however, explain it thus, in the person of God: I will not abandon you, I will not go to another nation; nor will I enter another city.

11:10.t: They will walk after the Lord; he will roar like a lion, for he himself will roar; and the sons of the sea will tremble, and they will fly like birds out of Egypt, and like a dove from the land of the Assyrians; and I will settle them in their houses, says the Lord. LXX: I will walk after the Lord; as a lion he will roar, for he himself will roar; and the sons of the waters will tremble, and they will fly like a bird out of Egypt, and like a dove from the land of the Assyrians; and I will settle them in their houses, says the Lord. When the Lord promises prosperous things, the people will be converted to him, and will walk after the Lord, because the Lord will roar like a lion. Of this the prophet Amos also makes mention: The Lord will roar from Zion, and from Jerusalem he will utter his voice. And he roars when he says: as Admah, I will set you as Zeboiim. And when he has roared, then the sons of the sea will tremble, or of the waters, as the LXX translated. […]

The Hebrews refer these things to the coming of Christ, whom they hope is yet to come. We show that they are already accomplished, because both from Egypt and from the Assyrians, that is, from the east and the west, and from the north and the south, they have come, and daily they come, who sit at table with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. And we can call sons of the sea, or of the waters, those who have been caught in the Lord's dragnet and drawn out of the sea of this world. And when they have been taken from death into life, they will be settled in their houses, which the Gospel calls barns, in which the chosen grain, separated from the chaff, is stored. It is said to be the nature of lions that when they growl and roar, all living creatures tremble, and, their step fixed, cannot move: so great is the terror, so great the dread. […]

11:12.t: Ephraim has surrounded me in his denial, and the house of Israel in deceit; but Judah went down as a witness with God, and faithful with the saints. LXX: Ephraim has surrounded me in falsehood, and the house of Israel and Judah in impiety; now God has known them, and the holy people of God will be called. The Hebrews hand down a tale of this kind: at the exodus of Israel from Egypt, when on one side the mountain, on another the Red Sea, and on another the army of Pharaoh hemmed them in, and the people were held shut in, while the other tribes despaired of safety and wished either to return to Egypt or to fight, Judah alone faithfully entered the sea, and for this reason he also merited to receive the kingdom. And this, they say, is what is now said: Judah, a witness of the words of God, his supporter and avenger, went down with God into the sea, and among the saints was most faithful, so as to believe the words of God who commanded. That is what they say. […]

12:1.t: Ephraim feeds on the wind and follows the burning heat; all day long he multiplies lying and devastation, and he has entered into a covenant with the Assyrians; and he was carrying oil into Egypt. LXX: But Ephraim, a most evil spirit, has pursued the burning heat; all day long he has multiplied vain and empty things, and he has made a covenant with the Assyrians; and he was trading oil in Egypt. Sacred history relates that Menahem, king of Israel, having made peace with Assyria, asked help of the Egyptians; and this is what is now said: that Ephraim feeds on winds, that is, deceives himself with vain hope, and follows καύσωνα, that is, the burning heat, and goes to the south, and does nothing else all day long but mock himself. And while he runs about this way and that, he prepares devastation and overthrow for his own cities. Is it not devastation and lying to have made a covenant with the Assyrians, and to have carried oil into Egypt? […]

12:2.t: Therefore the judgment of God is with Judah, and visitation upon Jacob; according to his ways and according to his devices he will repay him. In the womb he supplanted his brother, and in his strength he was directed with the angel; and he prevailed over the angel and was strengthened; he wept and besought him; in Bethel he found him, and there he spoke with us, and the Lord God of hosts. The Lord is his memorial; and you will turn to your God; keep mercy and judgment, and hope in your God always. LXX: And there is judgment for the Lord with Judah, that he may punish Jacob; according to his ways and according to his devices he will repay him. In the womb he supplanted his brother, and in his labor he prevailed with God, and he was strengthened with the angel, and was able; they wept and entreated me; in the house of ὢν they found me, and there it was spoken to them. But the Lord God almighty will be his memorial, and you will turn in your God; keep mercy and judgment; and draw near to your God always. […]

We can understand Judah as the churchman, who is rebuked by the Lord because he is not mindful of his former benefits toward him, but daily joins sins to sins; and he sets forth what those benefits are. When the Church, he says, was bringing you to birth in faith, you supplanted your brother, the Jew or the Gentile, and received his birthright; and in your strength you were directed with the angel, either overcoming the adverse powers, or strengthened by the blessings of the angel, who is himself God; and you prevailed in figure against the angel, so that you might prevail against men, and you were strengthened. And when you had won the victory, you wept and besought the angel of the Lord, and, remembering your old sins, you found him in Bethel, that is, in the house of God, which is the Church, or in the house of ὢν, of sorrow and tears and repentance. And that we might know who this Judah was, there, he says, he spoke with us, that is, with us Christians; […]

12:3.t: Moreover he sets forth how great benefits Judah, that is, Jacob, received, and the son is named in the father, and he recalls the ancient history, so that both the mercy of God toward Jacob and his hardness against God may be known. While he was still in Rebekah's womb, he supplanted his brother Esau, not indeed by his own strength, since he could not perceive it, but by the mercy of God, who knows and loves those whom he has predestined. And not only did he supplant his brother in the womb, but in his strength also he was directed with the angel, when at the torrent Jacob fought against the angel all night long. And because he was directed with the angel, he therefore received the name εὐθυτάτου, which in Hebrew is called isar, that is, of one directing, or directed.
